key: QR code stuck on a chai stall
name: ch00_upi_qr_everywhere
alt: A busy Indian street where a chai stall, vegetable cart, auto-rickshaw and kirana shop all display a printed QR code, with new uses like bill splitting and rent payment floating above.
scene: A wide street-level view of a lively Indian market lane in the morning, seen from slightly above so the whole row of sellers fits in. LEFT foreground: a small wooden chai stall with a dented aluminium kettle on a kerosene stove, a laminated paper QR code taped crookedly to the glass jar of biscuits; a young office-goer in a white shirt scans it with his phone while holding a cutting chai. CENTRE: a vegetable seller woman in her 50s in a green cotton sari sits behind a cart of tomatoes and onions, her own QR card hanging from a string on the cart handle; an elderly man pays her by phone. RIGHT: an auto-rickshaw parked with a QR sticker on the back of the driver seat, and beyond it a narrow kirana shop with a QR stand on the counter. Above the street float small rounded speech-bubble icons showing unplanned new uses: two friends splitting a restaurant bill, a tenant paying rent, a hand tipping a delivery boy. In the far background, faded and small, an old bank branch with a long queue and a card swipe machine gathering dust. Bright, cheerful daylight, a sense of sudden abundance. Labels: "PRINT A QR CODE" on a small banner above the chai stall, "NEW USES" beside the floating bubbles.

key: a ledger of seats per train per date
name: ch00_tatkal_rush_same_ledger
alt: Split illustration: a quiet old station clerk writing in a paper seat ledger, and the same ledger idea overwhelmed at 10 a.m. Tatkal opening with a huge crowd and servers.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a sleepy small-town railway booking office decades ago, a wooden counter with a brass bell, an elderly clerk in a khaki uniform and thick spectacles writing a passenger name into a thick cloth-bound register with ruled columns for train, date and seat; one traveller with a tin trunk waits patiently, a ceiling fan turns slowly and a calendar hangs on the wall. RIGHT panel: the same idea at modern scale at exactly ten in the morning, a large wall clock showing 10:00; hundreds of tiny people with phones and laptops form a giant funnel-shaped crowd pressing toward a single glowing digital ledger in the centre. Around the ledger, engineers in hoodies hold up signs and tools for the new solutions: a queue rope barrier, a stack of cached copies, a checkpoint gate and a valve marked to shed load. The same cloth register appears faintly inside the digital ledger to show the idea is unchanged. Calm warm lamplight on the left, intense bright blue light and motion lines on the right. Labels: "OLD IDEA" at the top of the left panel, "TATKAL RUSH" at the top of the right panel.

key: sitting with fifty players, groundsmen
name: ch00_cricket_manual_many_voices
alt: A cricket coach writes a batting manual surrounded by players, a groundsman, an umpire and a bat-maker, while feedback arrives on his phone from a club group.
scene: A single warm scene in a cricket club pavilion in the late afternoon, viewed from the doorway. In the centre, a grey-haired former cricketer in his late 50s, white club sweater over a collared shirt, sits at a long wooden table writing in a thick notebook titled "BATTING" with a pile of printed draft pages beside him. Around the table, people he has invited to talk: a young batter in pads holding a bat and demonstrating a stance, a weathered groundsman in a cap holding a roller handle, an umpire in a white coat and broad hat counting on his fingers, and a bat-maker in an apron showing a willow blade and a drawknife. Thin dotted lines run from each person's mouth to the notebook, showing their knowledge flowing in. In the foreground, the coach's phone lies on the table showing a club group chat with several message bubbles, one with a red cross through a sentence and a reply bubble saying "not true", representing pushback that gets fixed. Through the window behind, the green ground with players at the nets. Golden light, friendly collaborative mood. Labels: "DRAFT" on the stack of pages, "FEEDBACK" next to the phone.

key: why pressure cooks dal faster
name: ch00_cooking_teacher_any_cooker
alt: A cooking teacher explains how steam pressure cooks dal while students stand at three very different pressure cookers, all of which they can now use.
scene: A bright home cooking class in an Indian apartment kitchen, viewed from the front. On the left, a confident cooking teacher in her 40s, cotton salwar kameez with an apron and her hair tied back, points at a whiteboard showing a simple drawing of a pot with steam arrows pushing down on dal, a thermometer above water, and a small salt shaker icon, the principles she teaches. On the right counter stand three very different pressure cookers side by side: an old aluminium one with a whistle, a shiny steel one with a new kind of lid, and a modern electric one with a digital panel full of buttons. Three students, a college boy, a young mother and a retired uncle, each stand in front of a different cooker, confidently using it, each with a small thought bubble showing the same steam-and-pressure drawing from the whiteboard. A user manual for one cooker lies closed and ignored on the counter. Soft morning light from a window with a tulsi plant on the sill, calm and capable mood. Labels: "FUNDAMENTALS" on the whiteboard, "ANY COOKER" above the three cookers.

key: learning to cook from raw ingredients
name: ch00_raw_masala_vs_base_gravy
alt: Split illustration: a cook grinding masala from raw spices and testing recipes, versus a cook building dishes from a ready-made base gravy with instructions and finishing touches.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, two cooks in the same restaurant kitchen. LEFT panel: a young cook in his 20s with a cap and sweat on his brow kneels at a stone grinding slab crushing whole spices, red chillies, coriander seeds and cloves into fresh masala; behind him a row of test bowls with small chits labelled 1, 2, 3, 4 shows him repeating a recipe again and again, several crossed out. RIGHT panel: an older head cook in a white chef coat stands next to a huge steel pot of rich ready-made base gravy that came from elsewhere, labelled on a tag as the base; he hands a written order chit to a junior (instructions), drops a handful of fresh coriander and cream into a bowl (what you add at the end), and adjusts a small knob of salt (a small tweak), producing three different finished curries quickly. Between the panels, at the bottom, a restaurant pass window shows plates from both sides going out together, because the restaurant uses both. Warm yellow kitchen light, busy but orderly. Labels: "DMLS" at the top of the left panel, "AIE" at the top of the right panel.

key: pressure cooker and the tiffin box
name: ch00_lindy_cooker_tiffin_gadget
alt: A kitchen shelf through time: an old pressure cooker and tiffin box present across decades, while a flashy new gadget appears and is quickly thrown away.
scene: A wide kitchen-shelf scene shown as three side-by-side time slices of the same Indian kitchen wall, like a timeline strip, each slice with a small calendar on the wall. FIRST slice, faded sepia tones: a grandmother in a cotton sari places a dented steel pressure cooker and a round three-tier steel tiffin box on a wooden shelf. SECOND slice, warmer colours: a mother in her 30s uses the same pressure cooker, whistle steaming, and packs the same style of tiffin box for a schoolchild in uniform. THIRD slice, bright modern kitchen with a tiled wall: a young man takes the same cooker and tiffin off the shelf, while on the counter a flashy colourful gadget with blinking lights and a big sticker reading "NEW!" sits half unboxed, and a dustbin beside it already contains two similar abandoned gadgets. A long arrow runs along the bottom of all three slices under the cooker and tiffin, showing they have lasted decades; a very short arrow sits only under the gadget. Warm nostalgic light that becomes crisp at the right. Labels: "SURVIVED DECADES" under the long arrow, "SURVIVED MONTHS" under the short arrow.

key: a guide to running a restaurant
name: ch00_restaurant_guide_not_oven_manual
alt: Three books on a counter: a restaurant-running guide in focus, beside a cooking-school textbook and a single oven manual, with a restaurateur choosing an oven for a menu.
scene: A restaurant owner's small back office, viewed over her shoulder. She is in her 30s, wearing a crisp kurta and reading glasses, sitting at a desk with a menu card pinned to the wall listing a few dishes. On the desk lie three books side by side. The one she is reading is thick and well-used, open to a page with simple drawings of a dining room, kitchen layout, three different ovens with tick marks beside the one that fits her menu, and arrows linking menu dishes to the right oven. To its left, a fat cooking-school textbook with a drawing of boiling water on the cover sits closed and pushed aside, implying she already knows the basics. To its right, a thin manual for a single brand of oven, also closed, with a picture of one oven and its buttons. Through the office doorway, the kitchen is visible with two ovens and a cook waiting for her decision. One page of the open book has a small folded corner with a warning triangle, where it goes deep into the oven's wiring. Calm late-morning light, practical and decisive mood. Labels: "RUN THE RESTAURANT" on the open book, "ONE OVEN" on the thin manual.

key: like opening a chai stall
name: ch00_chai_stall_three_steps
alt: Three-panel strip: deciding whether to open a chai stall, learning how tea and milk behave when boiled, and tasting every batch while asking customers.
scene: A three-panel comic strip read left to right, the same young stall owner in all three: a man in his mid-20s with a moustache, a checked half-sleeve shirt and a towel over his shoulder. PANEL ONE: he stands on a busy street corner near a bus stop, scratching his head, looking at two options drawn as thought bubbles, an expensive shiny espresso-style machine with a price tag and a simple kerosene stove with a kettle; a small tick appears beside the stove. PANEL TWO: inside a tiny stall, he leans over a boiling pan of milk and tea leaves, watching the colour change and the milk rise, a magnifying-glass inset showing tea leaves unfurling and milk foam, a notebook beside him with arrows. PANEL THREE: the stall is open, he pours chai from a height into small glasses, sips one himself with eyes half closed, while two customers, an auto driver and a student, give a thumbs up and a so-so hand gesture; a little chalkboard on the stall shows tally marks. Warm morning light, homely and hopeful mood. Labels: "SHOULD I?" above panel one, "KNOW THE TEA" above panel two, "TASTE EVERY BATCH" above panel three.

key: first a narrow-gauge track
name: ch01_railway_line_four_stages
alt: A railway line shown in four stages from left to right: narrow gauge, broad gauge, electrified track, and a busy junction served by many operators.
scene: A long horizontal panorama of one railway line running from left to right across a rolling Indian landscape, built in four visible stages separated by small milestone posts. FIRST stretch at the far left: a thin narrow-gauge track through hills with a tiny toy-like steam engine pulling two small coaches. SECOND stretch: the track widens into broad gauge with heavier sleepers, and a long diesel goods train with many wagons rolls along easily; a small gang of track workers in orange vests waves as it passes, showing the heavier loads now fit. THIRD stretch: overhead electric wires and steel masts appear above the track, and a sleek electric train carries mixed cargo, open wagons holding a large picture frame, a loudspeaker and stacks of books, meaning images, audio and text all ride the same line. FOURTH stretch at the far right: a busy junction station with several platforms, a big departure board full of rows, and trains in different colours run by different operators, passengers with suitcases bustling. Clear afternoon light, a sense of steady progress. Labels: "LANGUAGE MODELS" under the first stretch, "FOUNDATION MODELS" under the third stretch, "AI ENGINEERING" under the junction.

key: Hindi/Devanagari typeset tray
name: ch01_devanagari_typeset_tray
alt: A typesetter picks syllable blocks from a wooden tray of Devanagari type to compose a word, showing tokens as reusable pieces between letters and whole words.
scene: A close, slightly overhead view of an old printing press workshop in a small Indian town. In the centre, an elderly typesetter in his 60s with half-moon spectacles, a white vest and a cloth tied around his waist, stands at a large slanted wooden type case divided into many small compartments. Each compartment holds metal type blocks, and the blocks are visibly not single strokes and not whole words but common syllable pieces of Devanagari script. With tweezers he lifts three blocks and sets them into a composing stick in his other hand, where they join into one longer word. An inset circle at the top right shows three rows comparing sizes: a row of tiny single strokes, a row of medium syllable blocks highlighted, and a row of long whole-word bars. On a side table lies a freshly printed sheet with a new word nobody has printed before, made from the same blocks. Ink stains on his fingers, a hanging bulb and paper stacks in the background. Warm amber workshop light, patient and precise mood. Labels: "TOKENS" above the type case, "NEW WORD" beside the printed sheet.

key: Each singer must start a song
name: ch01_antakshari_vs_crossword
alt: Split illustration: friends playing antakshari, each singing from the last letter of the previous song, versus a person filling a crossword blank using letters on both sides.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a family evening on a living-room floor with cushions, five relatives sitting in a circle playing antakshari, a teenage girl in a T-shirt mid-song with one hand raised, an uncle in a kurta clapping, an aunt laughing, and a grandmother on a low chair keeping score on a notepad. Above them, a chain of speech bubbles runs left to right like a train, each bubble ending in a letter that is circled and passed with a curved arrow into the start of the next bubble; a big arrow behind the girl points only backwards to the previous bubble, showing she can only look back. RIGHT panel: a retired man in a sweater with a newspaper folded on a desk, pencil in hand, solving a crossword; the grid has one empty square highlighted, with small arrows coming into it from letters on its left and right sides and from above and below. Soft lamp light on both sides, cosy evening mood. Labels: "LOOK BACK ONLY" above the left panel, "BOTH SIDES" above the right panel.

key: covers the next word of a newspaper line
name: ch01_newspaper_dictation_free_labels
alt: A teacher covers the next word of a newspaper line with a card while students guess it, with stacks of newspapers behind serving as free answer keys.
scene: A government school classroom with green walls and wooden benches, viewed from the back of the room. At the front, a cheerful teacher in her 40s in a printed cotton sari holds a large newspaper against the blackboard and slides a plain white card along one printed line, covering the next word. Students in white-and-blue uniforms raise hands eagerly, each with a small speech bubble showing a different guess. Under the card, visible only to the viewer through a small cut-away inset, is the true word, showing the newspaper itself holds the answer. Along the side wall of the classroom, tall stacks of newspapers in many languages are piled to the ceiling, with a hand-written sign on the stack reading "free homework", and a crate in the corridor outside with even more bundles arriving on a cycle cart. No red pen or answer sheet is in sight, and the teacher's own table holds only a cup of tea and an attendance register. Bright morning light through tall windows, lively mood. Labels: "NEXT WORD?" on the white card, "ANSWER KEY" on the newspaper stacks.

key: A big steel almirah vs a small one
name: ch01_almirah_capacity_vs_clothes
alt: Split illustration: five shirts lost inside a huge steel almirah, versus the same five shirts fitting neatly in a small almirah.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same small rented bedroom, divided by a thin vertical line. A young man in his 20s in a vest and track pants appears in both halves. LEFT panel: an enormous grey steel almirah, taller than the door, with both doors open, dominates the cramped room; inside, five shirts hang lonely on one rod with vast empty shelves, and the man stands beside it scratching his head, holding a receipt with a large price and his wallet empty, the bed squeezed into a corner. RIGHT panel: the same room with a small single-door steel almirah against the wall; the same five shirts fill it neatly, the room feels spacious, the man sits relaxed on the bed reading. In the far background of the right panel, through the doorway, a delivery van is unloading many cardboard boxes of clothes, hinting that a big almirah only pays off once there are many clothes. Soft afternoon light. Labels: "BIG MODEL" above the left almirah, "SMALL MODEL" above the right almirah, "LITTLE DATA" on a tag on the five shirts.

key: every photo already has a caption
name: ch01_newspaper_archive_captions
alt: A newspaper archive room where every photo already has a printed caption beneath it, so pairs of picture and text are collected without hiring anyone to describe them.
scene: A vast newspaper archive room in an old Indian newspaper office, viewed from a high corner. Tall metal shelves stretch into the distance, packed with bound volumes. In the foreground, a long wooden table is covered with clipped newspaper photos, each photo with its printed caption strip directly underneath: a cricket match, a monsoon flood street, a wedding procession, an elephant at a temple. A young archivist in her late 20s, cotton kurta and a lanyard, scans the clippings with a flatbed scanner, and each scan appears on a monitor as a neat pair, picture on the left and caption text on the right, joined by a small link icon. A mountain of such pairs grows on the screen. In the corner, an empty chair with a sign reading "describer" shows nobody had to be hired to write descriptions. One clipping's caption reads only "look at this" with exclamation marks, a hint that some captions are noisy. Dusty warm light through high windows, quiet and industrious mood. Labels: "PHOTO + CAPTION" above the monitor, "FREE LABELS" on the table edge.

key: training a specialist from childhood
name: ch01_graduate_vs_childhood_specialist
alt: Split illustration: a versatile graduate given instructions, company files and a training course, versus a specialist trained since childhood for one narrow job.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a modern office, a smart fresh graduate in her early 20s in a formal shirt and lanyard stands at a desk surrounded by three helpers: a manager hands her a written instruction sheet, a clerk wheels in a trolley of company files, and a poster on the wall advertises a short training course with a calendar circled. Around her head float small icons of the many jobs she could do: a pen, a calculator, a speech bubble, a globe. RIGHT panel: a narrow workshop where a middle-aged man in overalls who has trained since childhood does one task, fitting watch gears with a loupe on his eye; on the wall behind him a faded series of framed photos shows him as a boy, a teenager and an adult at the same bench. His workstation is small and costs little to run, a single lamp and a single tool rack. Daylight office on the left, focused lamplight on the right. Labels: "FOUNDATION MODEL" above the graduate, "TASK MODEL" above the specialist, "PROMPT, FILES, COURSE" beside the three helpers.

key: swallowed the camera, the map
name: ch01_smartphone_swallowed_gadgets
alt: A smartphone in the centre pulling in a camera, paper map, torch, wallet and train ticket, while a crowd of different people all reach for phones.
scene: A central illustration of a single large smartphone standing upright like a doorway in the middle of the frame. Around it, in a circle, older separate objects are being drawn into the phone along curved motion trails: a film camera, a folded paper road map, a heavy torch, a leather wallet with coins and notes, a printed train ticket, a landline phone receiver and a wristwatch. Each object shrinks slightly as it approaches the screen and appears as a small icon on the phone's home screen. In the lower foreground, a diverse crowd of people reach toward the phone with interest: a schoolgirl, a farmer in a turban, a delivery rider, an elderly lady with a walking stick and an office worker, showing that more abilities meant more people needed one; a few hold out old basic phones and look tempted. In the faded background, an empty old shop counter selling torches and maps has a closed shutter. Bright, upbeat midday light, a feeling of things converging. Labels: "ONE DEVICE, MANY JOBS" above the phone, "MORE USERS" under the crowd.

key: anyone with a good recipe can sell
name: ch01_shared_kitchen_model_api
alt: Split illustration: an expensive restaurant needing rented premises and hired chefs, versus a home cook selling from a shared kitchen through a delivery app from day one.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel labelled as the old way: a would-be restaurant owner, a man in his 30s with a folder of papers, stands in front of an empty rented shop with a big lease agreement, a pile of bills, a contractor measuring the walls and three chefs waiting for salaries; he looks overwhelmed, with a calendar showing months crossed off before opening. RIGHT panel: a young woman in her late 20s, sleeves rolled up, cooks her family recipe in one bay of a large shared commercial kitchen, a row of identical bays with other cooks beside her using the same shared stoves, fridges and dishwashers. A delivery rider with an insulated bag on a scooter picks up her packed boxes at the window, and a phone stand on her counter shows new order notifications arriving on day one. In the background, many other cooks in the shared kitchen are making similar dishes from similar recipe books, hinting that standing out gets harder. Dim heavy light on the left, bright hopeful light on the right. Labels: "BUILD IT YOURSELF" above the left panel, "SHARED KITCHEN" above the right panel.

key: text in, text out: very exposed
name: ch01_translator_vs_cook_exposure
alt: Split illustration: a translator whose whole day is papers in and papers out with a helper halving the pile, versus a cook working with fire and hands that no helper can halve.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a translator in her 40s in a cotton kurta and spectacles sits at a desk in a small office, an in-tray of documents in one language and an out-tray of translated documents in another; a robot-like helper with a friendly face stands beside her desk taking half the pile and producing drafts quickly, and a wall clock shows her finishing early. A big arrow runs from in-tray through the helper to the out-tray. RIGHT panel: a dhaba cook in his 50s, sweat on his forehead, flips rotis on a hot tawa over open flame, tastes dal from a ladle and adjusts the fire with his hand; the same robot-like helper stands nearby holding a book, looking confused, unable to do anything, while the clock shows the same long day. Small gauge dials at the top of each panel show the share of the day the helper can cut: almost full on the left, empty on the right. Warm office light on the left, orange firelight on the right. Labels: "HIGH EXPOSURE" above the left gauge, "ZERO EXPOSURE" above the right gauge.

key: A power drill for a carpenter
name: ch01_carpenter_power_drill
alt: A carpenter drills holes quickly with a power drill, while the cupboard design on paper and the hidden wiring in the wall still need his own judgement.
scene: An apartment room under renovation, viewed from a slight angle. A carpenter in his 40s with a pencil behind his ear, a sleeveless sweater over a checked shirt and sawdust on his forearms, holds a cordless power drill and zips through a row of neat holes in a wooden plank on two sawhorses; a little motion blur and a counter bubble show many holes done in seconds, with a hand drill lying unused nearby. Behind him on the wall, a half-built cupboard frame is marked with pencil lines, and a rolled-out paper design of the full cupboard with measurements is pinned up; he glances at it thoughtfully, one hand on his chin, because the drill cannot design it. On the wall, a cut-away inset view reveals electrical wires running hidden inside the plaster near where the next hole is marked with a red X, showing the danger only the craftsman's knowledge can avoid. A young apprentice holds a tape measure and watches. Warm afternoon light through dusty air, focused working mood. Labels: "FAST HOLES" next to the drill, "DESIGN" on the paper plan, "HIDDEN WIRES" on the cut-away inset.

key: never draws the same pattern twice
name: ch01_rangoli_never_twice
alt: Split illustration: a rangoli artist happily creating a different pattern at each doorway, versus a bank clerk horrified that the same statement prints differently every time.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: an apartment corridor during Diwali, a young woman in a festive silk sari kneels on the floor with a plate of coloured powders, drawing a vivid rangoli at a doorway; along the corridor three earlier doorways each show a completely different rangoli design, a lotus, a peacock and a geometric star, and neighbours stand admiring them with smiles and diyas glowing. RIGHT panel: a quiet bank branch, a bespectacled clerk in a tie holds up three printed account statements for the same customer side by side, and each one shows different numbers and a different layout; his eyes are wide in alarm, and an elderly customer across the counter frowns, clutching a passbook. A small question mark hovers over the stack, and a printer behind the clerk is spitting out yet another version with a third set of figures. Warm golden festival glow on the left, cool fluorescent office light on the right. Labels: "VARIETY IS GOOD" above the left panel, "VARIETY IS A DISASTER" above the right panel.

key: typing clerk outside the district court
name: ch01_court_typist_affidavit
alt: A typing clerk outside a district court drafts an affidavit from a villager's rough story, and the villager reads and corrects one line before signing.
scene: The busy compound outside an Indian district court in the late morning, viewed at eye level. Under a tin shed against the boundary wall, a typing clerk in his 50s with a neat moustache, white half-sleeve shirt and spectacles sits on a plastic chair at a small table with a computer and a printer, stacks of stamp paper and a rubber stamp beside him. Across the table, a farmer in his 40s in a dhoti and a folded towel on his shoulder tells his story with expressive hands, a speech bubble showing a rough sketch of a field boundary and a broken fence. In a second moment shown on the right side of the same scene, the farmer holds the printed affidavit close to his face, pointing at one line with his finger, and the clerk leans in to correct it with a pen before the farmer signs at the bottom. In the background, lawyers in black coats walk past, a row of similar typing sheds lines the wall, and a peon carries files. Bright, dusty midday light, practical and everyday mood. Labels: "ROUGH STORY" beside the speech bubble, "YOU CHECK" next to the farmer pointing at the line.

key: makes a fresh worksheet each evening
name: ch01_home_tutor_fresh_worksheet
alt: A home tuition teacher hands a child a fresh worksheet made only for his weak chapter, while many other children in the neighbourhood each get their own tutor.
scene: An evening scene in a modest Indian home, viewed from the doorway. At a small study table under a tube light, a kind tuition teacher in her 30s in a simple kurta and a shawl sits beside a ten-year-old boy in a school T-shirt. She hands him a freshly written worksheet, and an inset bubble above shows the boy's report card with one subject, fractions, circled in red, and the worksheet full of fraction pizza drawings matching exactly that weak chapter. On the table, yesterday's worksheet on a different topic lies marked with ticks. Through the open window behind them, the scene widens to a row of neighbouring houses at night; in every lit window a different child sits with a small friendly glowing tutor figure beside them, showing one personal teacher for every child instead of only for families who can pay. The boy's mother peeks from the kitchen doorway, pleased. Warm yellow interior light against a blue dusk outside, tender and hopeful mood. Labels: "JUST FOR YOU" on the worksheet, "ONE FOR EVERYONE" above the row of windows.

key: help desk that never closes
name: ch01_railway_helpdesk_handoff
alt: A railway help desk answers a quick ticket-status question instantly, while a worried man whose mother is stranded is guided to a human officer.
scene: A large railway station concourse at night, viewed from slightly above. On the left, a bright digital help kiosk with a friendly screen face and speech bubbles in several scripts answers a young traveller in a hoodie who holds up a ticket; a small clock bubble shows one second, and he walks away satisfied with a thumbs up. In the middle, a long queue of other passengers with suitcases moves quickly past the kiosk. On the right, a distressed middle-aged man in a sweater, phone pressed to his ear, gestures anxiously; a thought bubble shows his elderly mother sitting alone on a bench at a distant dark platform with her bag. The kiosk screen shows a glowing arrow pointing him toward a small glass cabin where a uniformed human railway officer, a calm woman in her 40s, stands up to help him. Above the kiosk hangs a big station clock reading 2 a.m., showing the desk never closes. Cool night lighting with a warm pool of light in the officer's cabin. Labels: "INSTANT ANSWERS" above the kiosk, "HAND OFF" along the arrow to the officer.

key: reads all circulars and tells you
name: ch01_peon_three_circulars
alt: An office peon sorts a huge pile of circulars and hands an officer just the three that matter, with a thin thread linking each back to its original.
scene: A government office room with steel almirahs and a ceiling fan, viewed from the side. On the left, a mountain of paper circulars spills off a desk and onto the floor, held with bulldog clips and stamped with official seals. An office peon in his 50s in a khaki uniform with a pen behind his ear sits on a stool reading through the pile at speed, tossing most sheets into a large wire basket. On the right, a busy officer in a crisp shirt sits at her desk with a file, and the peon hands her exactly three neat sheets, each with a short handwritten note on top. From each of the three summary sheets, a thin red thread runs back across the room to the matching original circular in the pile, a visible way back to the source. One thread is snipped, with a small warning sign near it, showing what happens without a link back. A tea glass and a rubber stamp sit on the officer's desk. Warm afternoon light through dusty blinds, quiet efficient mood. Labels: "SUMMARY" above the three sheets, "SOURCE" on the threads near the pile.

key: 40,000 unsorted family photos
name: ch01_shoebox_vs_labelled_album
alt: Split illustration: a woman lost in a shoebox of unsorted family photos, versus a neat album where every photo carries a label and she finds the right one instantly.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same woman in her 30s in a cotton salwar suit in both halves, sitting on a living-room floor. LEFT panel: she is surrounded by overflowing shoeboxes and a sea of loose printed photos spilling across the carpet, beaches, weddings, birthdays all jumbled; she holds one photo up with a frustrated face, a thought bubble asking where the beach photo with grandmother is. RIGHT panel: she sits calmly with a tidy photo album open on her lap, every photo with a neat small tag beneath it; she points straight at one showing an elderly grandmother in a sari on a sunny beach, tagged "GOA 2019, DADI". A small friendly robot-like helper sits beside her with a label maker in hand, a neat stack of finished albums on the shelf behind them. In the corner of the right panel, one photo has slipped behind the album with a wrong tag, almost hidden, a quiet hint that a mislabelled photo goes missing. Warm afternoon light. Labels: "UNSORTED" above the left panel, "LABELLED" above the right panel.

key: actually calls, books, and puts it
name: ch01_assistant_books_table
alt: A personal assistant phones a restaurant, books a table and writes it in her employer's diary, rather than just reading out a phone number.
scene: A two-part scene in a small modern office, read from left to right. LEFT part: a busy businessman in his 40s in a blazer, talking on a second phone, waves a hand toward his assistant with a speech bubble showing a plate and a fork, asking for a dinner booking. In a small faded inset beneath him, a plain search box simply shows a phone number with nothing else happening, the old way. RIGHT part: the assistant, a capable young woman in her late 20s in a formal kurta with a headset, actually does the work in a sequence of three small actions linked by arrows: dialling the restaurant on a desk phone with a speech bubble saying "table for four", typing the confirmation into a laptop, and writing the booking into a leather desk diary open at Friday with a red pen. Next to her keyboard sits a company credit card with a small padlock and a sticky note reading "ask first", showing real actions with real consequences. Bright office daylight, efficient mood. Labels: "JUST INFORMS" on the faded inset, "ACTS" above the assistant's three-step sequence.

key: A family-run travel agency
name: ch01_travel_agency_three_levels
alt: A family-run travel agency shown at three levels of urgency: losing customers to phones and building online presence, buying a messaging tool, and a nephew experimenting on weekends.
scene: A cross-section of a small family-run travel agency in a market building, shown as three stacked floors from bottom to top. GROUND floor, most urgent: the owner, a worried man in his 50s in a safari suit, watches customers walk past his posters while staring at their phones; he and his daughter are urgently setting up a laptop and a website mock-up on a big screen, sleeves rolled up. MIDDLE floor: two staff members at desks happily use a simple bought messaging tool that sends ready-made trip reminders, a stack of paper chits replaced by a neat screen, a clock showing time saved. TOP floor, the attic: a teenage nephew in a hoodie on a beanbag on a Sunday tinkers with a laptop and sticky notes, a calendar marked with weekend dates, a relaxed curious mood. A tall arrow on the right side of the building runs from the ground floor up, showing the urgency falling. Late afternoon light through windows, layered and orderly composition. Labels: "LEVEL 1" on the ground floor, "LEVEL 2" on the middle floor, "LEVEL 3" on the top floor.

key: A paan shop next to a big mall
name: ch01_paan_shop_beside_mall
alt: A small paan shop beside a big shopping mall survives because the paan-wala knows every regular customer's exact order, while the mall's own counter waits empty.
scene: A busy city corner at dusk, viewed from across the road. On the right, a huge glass shopping mall towers with bright lights, escalators visible inside and a big entrance; just inside the entrance stands a shiny new paan counter staffed by a bored young attendant with no customers. On the left, in the shadow of the mall, a tiny wooden paan shop with hanging strings of supari packets and a small lamp; the paan-wala, a cheerful man in his 60s with a white vest and a red-stained smile, is already preparing a paan before the customer arrives. Three regulars approach, an office clerk, an auto driver and a retired professor, and each has a small bubble above the paan-wala's head showing their exact personal order, sweet, plain, extra elaichi. A notebook hangs on a nail with the regulars' names and preferences, and a faded board shows the shop's founding year. Warm golden lamp glow on the small shop against the cold white light of the mall. Labels: "KNOWS EVERY ORDER" above the paan shop, "DISTRIBUTION" above the mall entrance.

key: your lunch arrives hot, on time
name: ch01_dabbawala_promise_metrics
alt: A dabbawala delivers a hot tiffin to an office desk on time, with four small gauges showing count, speed, cost and the customer's satisfaction.
scene: A bright city office at exactly lunchtime, viewed from the aisle. A dabbawala in his 40s wearing a white boat-shaped cap, white kurta and pyjama, with a long wooden crate of tiffins balanced on his shoulder, places a round steel tiffin carrier on a young accountant's desk; steam rises from the opened top box showing dal and rice, and the accountant smiles gratefully, a wall clock behind reading one o'clock. Through the window, a suburban train and a line of other dabbawalas with bicycles and crates can be seen. Along the bottom of the scene, four small round gauges sit like a dashboard: one with a stack of tiffins for count, one with a stopwatch for speed, one with a rupee coin for cost, and one with a smiling face for satisfaction, all pointing into the green. The tiffin lid has a coded colour marking painted on it, and a colleague at the next desk is still waiting with an empty plate, glancing at the clock. Warm midday light, proud and dependable mood. Labels: "HOT, ON TIME, AT YOUR DESK" on a banner above the scene, "METRICS" beside the row of gauges.

key: the walls and roof go up in weeks
name: ch01_house_shell_vs_finishing
alt: Split illustration: a house shell with walls and roof up in a few weeks, versus months of plumbing, wiring, tiling and fixing leaks inside the same house.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same two-storey Indian house under construction in both halves, with a calendar pinned to a pillar in each. LEFT panel: bright and fast, the brick walls and concrete roof are complete, bamboo scaffolding still stands, a cheerful contractor in a white shirt and helmet gives a thumbs up to the owner couple, and the calendar shows only three weeks torn off; from outside the house looks almost done. RIGHT panel: the cut-away interior of the same house, slow and messy, a plumber lying under a sink wrestling with pipes, an electrician on a ladder pulling tangled wires from a wall chase, a tiler on his knees with spacers and a bucket of grout, and a dripping ceiling with a bucket catching drops while a worker searches for the leak with a torch; the owner couple looks tired, the wife holding a long checklist, and the calendar on the pillar shows many months torn away, a heap of torn sheets on the floor. Cement dust in the air, a half-fitted door leaning against a wall. Bright clear light on the left, dimmer dusty light on the right. Labels: "LOOKS DONE" above the left panel, "THE REAL WORK" above the right panel.

key: on a road under construction
name: ch01_shop_on_road_works
alt: Three panels of the same roadside shop during road works: a new flyover brings customers, a diversion forces a moved signboard, and a notice bans shops on the stretch.
scene: A three-panel strip of the same small roadside snack shop and its owner, a man in his 40s with a moustache, a printed shirt and a cash tin, as road works change the street around him. PANEL ONE: a brand-new flyover has opened nearby and its exit ramp lands right in front of his shop; a crowd of new customers with bikes and cars stops to buy samosas, and he beams while frying. PANEL TWO: orange barricades and a big diversion arrow now send traffic down a side lane; the owner, sleeves rolled up, is carrying his tall painted signboard on his shoulder to the corner of the side lane so passing drivers can still see it, determined but sweaty. PANEL THREE: a municipal notice board has been nailed to a post in front of the shop with a large red symbol of a crossed-out shop, and an official in a cap points at it while the owner stares in shock, the shutter half down. In the background of every panel, construction cranes and dust. Midday sun in the first two panels, grey overcast sky in the third. Labels: "GOOD CHANGE" above panel one, "ADAPT" above panel two, "FATAL" above panel three.

key: the building, gas line and cold storage
name: ch01_restaurant_three_layers
alt: A cut-away restaurant in three layers: the dining room and menu at the top, the kitchen in the middle, and the building, gas line and cold storage at the bottom.
scene: A cut-away side view of a three-level Indian restaurant building, like a doll's house with the front wall removed. TOP level: a bright dining room with families at tables, a waiter in a vest handing over a large new menu card full of dishes from different cuisines, decorative lamps and a cashier counter; this level is busy with change, new menu boards being hung by a worker on a stool. MIDDLE level: the kitchen, cooks in caps working at tandoors and woks, new recipe sheets clipped above the stations, a head chef tasting from a ladle, also clearly changing with new cuisines. BOTTOM level: the basement with the building's foundations, thick yellow gas pipes running along the wall to a valve, a big walk-in cold storage room with frosty doors, an electrical panel and a water tank; a single maintenance man in overalls checks a gauge, and everything here looks old, steady and unchanged, with a dust-covered plaque showing the year it was installed. Beside the top level, a delivery rider receives a ready-made dish passed straight from outside, skipping the kitchen. Warm light upstairs, cool steady light in the basement. Labels: "APPLICATION" beside the dining room, "MODEL" beside the kitchen, "INFRASTRUCTURE" beside the basement.

key: Driving a car vs being a mechanic
name: ch01_driver_vs_mechanic_ghat
alt: A driver confidently drives a car up a ghat road until a strange noise starts, and a mechanic at a roadside garage diagnoses the engine.
scene: A winding ghat road through green hills with a deep valley on one side, shown in two moments side by side. LEFT half: a confident young driver in her late 20s, sunglasses pushed up on her head, steers a small hatchback smoothly around a hairpin bend, a family relaxed in the back seat, road signs warning of sharp curves; she clearly drives very well without knowing anything about the gearbox. RIGHT half, a little further up the road: the same car pulled over at a small roadside garage with a tin roof and old tyres stacked outside; jagged sound lines and a small question mark come from under the bonnet. A mechanic in his 50s in oil-stained overalls and a cloth cap leans into the engine bay with a torch, head tilted, listening, and an inset bubble shows a cut-away of the engine with one worn belt glowing red. The driver stands beside him, curious, holding the car keys. A shelf of spare parts and a calendar hang inside the garage. Bright morning light on the hills and soft mist in the valley. Labels: "DRIVER" above the left half, "MECHANIC" above the garage.

key: sticky note on your monitor for today
name: ch01_school_induction_sticky_note
alt: A four-step strip of one person's learning: years of schooling, a company induction, a team lead's coaching, and a sticky note on the monitor for today's task.
scene: A four-step horizontal strip showing the same person growing up, linked by arrows from left to right, each step smaller in size than the one before to show how much each one changes the person. STEP ONE, the largest: a schoolgirl in a navy uniform with a heavy backpack walks through a school gate under a tall stack of textbooks representing twelve years of study. STEP TWO: now a young woman of about 22 in formal clothes, she sits in a company training hall with other new joiners, a presenter at a screen showing the company's way of serving customers. STEP THREE: at a team desk, a friendly team lead in his 30s with a lanyard leans over her shoulder, pointing at her screen and teaching the team's own conventions. STEP FOUR, the smallest: a close-up of her monitor edge with a single yellow sticky note reading "today: refund email"; a faint dotted outline shows the note will be peeled off and thrown away at the end of the day, while the earlier steps are drawn solidly, as they stay inside her. Soft daylight throughout, steady and encouraging mood. Labels: "PRE-TRAINING" under step one, "FINETUNING" under step three, "PROMPT" under step four.

key: Grading an MCQ paper vs grading essays
name: ch01_mcq_vs_essay_grading
alt: Split illustration: an MCQ answer sheet graded quickly with one key that everyone agrees on, versus two examiners giving different marks to the same essay.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves inside a board exam evaluation centre. LEFT panel: a young examiner in a cardigan lays a transparent answer-key stencil over a bubble-sheet, and every shaded circle lines up perfectly; a tall pile of checked sheets beside her grows quickly, a wall clock shows very little time passing, and two colleagues glance at the same sheet nodding in agreement. RIGHT panel: two older examiners, a stern man with grey hair and a gentle woman with reading glasses, sit side by side reading photocopies of the same handwritten essay answer, many pages long; he has written a low mark in red on his copy and she has written a much higher mark in green on hers, and they stare at each other in disagreement. A small pile of unread essays towers behind them and the clock on their wall shows hours gone. Fluorescent hall light, ceiling fans and steel cupboards in the background. Labels: "ONE KEY" above the left panel, "TWO OPINIONS" above the right panel.

key: reread the whole page before each
name: ch01_typist_rereads_page
alt: A typist types one letter at a time and must reread the whole page before each new letter, so a long letter takes very long.
scene: An old-fashioned typing office with wooden desks, viewed from the side. In the centre, a typist in his 30s with neatly combed hair, a white shirt and sleeve garters sits at a heavy manual typewriter. He presses a single key with one finger; above his head a looping arrow shows his eyes travelling back over every line already typed on the page before he can type the next letter. A sequence of small ghosted copies of him behind his chair shows him repeating this loop again and again: read the whole page, type one letter, read the whole page, type one letter. On the desk, a short note is already finished, while a long letter spills off the typewriter roller onto the floor, only half typed, with the wall clock behind showing evening. A colleague at the next desk peeks over, yawning. An inset bubble in the corner shows a small bookmark-like card listing the lines already read, hinting that a clever shortcut could save the rereading. Soft late-afternoon light through blinds, patient but weary mood. Labels: "ONE LETTER AT A TIME" above the typewriter, "REREAD" along the looping arrow.

key: open-book exam with 32 solved examples
name: ch01_open_vs_closed_book_marks
alt: Split illustration: one student writes an open-book exam with a thick folder of solved examples, while another writes a closed-book exam with only a few, and their marks are compared unfairly.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, two students in two different exam halls. LEFT panel: a boy in a striped school shirt sits at a desk with a thick open folder of solved examples beside his answer sheet, thirty-two tabbed pages fanning out, a relaxed expression as he copies the method. RIGHT panel: a girl in a plain school shirt sits at a bare desk with only a small card of five worked examples, writing carefully, focused and determined. Above both panels, spanning across the dividing line, a notice board displays two mark sheets pinned next to each other, the boy's with a higher number circled as topper; but a large magnifying glass hovers over the small fine print at the bottom of each mark sheet, showing the different exam rules. A puzzled parent stands in front of the notice board, comparing them. Bright morning light in both halls, rows of desks and ceiling fans. Labels: "OPEN BOOK" above the left panel, "CLOSED BOOK" above the right panel, "READ THE FINE PRINT" beside the magnifying glass.

key: Briefing a new site engineer
name: ch01_site_engineer_briefing
alt: A new site engineer is briefed with a job sheet, drawings and soil report, a toolbox, and the site diary, at a construction site.
scene: A construction site office in a portacabin at the edge of a building site, viewed through its open door. A newly arrived site engineer in her late 20s, wearing a white hard hat, a reflective vest and boots, stands at a plywood table being briefed by an older project manager in his 50s with a grey moustache. On the table, four clearly separate items are laid out in a row, each picked up in turn: a one-page job sheet with a bulleted task, a roll of blueprints and a soil report folder with sample jars of earth, a red metal toolbox with spirit level, measuring tape and hammer, and a thick worn site diary open to handwritten entries from previous weeks. Through the window behind them, a half-built concrete frame and a tower crane are visible. A small inset in the corner shows the same engineer without the diary, standing in front of a wall with a confused question mark, guessing. Bright morning sun, purposeful mood. Labels: "INSTRUCTIONS" on the job sheet, "CONTEXT" on the blueprints, "MEMORY" on the site diary.

key: bake a batch at home, sell it
name: ch01_home_batch_before_factory
alt: Split illustration: the old way of building a biscuit factory before knowing if anyone buys, versus baking a home batch, selling at a Sunday market, and only then building the factory.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel, the old way, shown as a sequence top to bottom: a huge new biscuit factory with chimneys is built first, then a designer at a drawing board sketches a biscuit, and finally a shop shelf of unsold biscuit packets gathers dust, with the worried owner in a suit standing beside it. RIGHT panel, the new way, shown as a sequence top to bottom: a woman in her 30s in an apron bakes a tray of biscuits in her home oven, then sells them at a lively Sunday market stall with a hand-painted board and a queue of returning customers holding empty tins for refills, and only at the bottom a factory outline drawn as a dotted blueprint with a tick, built after demand is proven. In a small corner of the right panel, a few hidden problems are drawn as tiny cracks under the market table: a rupee sign, a stopwatch and a broken biscuit, problems that appear only at scale. Grey industrial light on the left, cheerful market sunshine on the right. Labels: "FACTORY FIRST" above the left panel, "PRODUCT FIRST" above the right panel.

key: Buying a second-hand car. You
name: ch02_secondhand_car_inspection
alt: A buyer inspects a second-hand car, with callouts linking where it was driven, its engine, its service history and the driver's style to training data, architecture, post-training and sampling.
scene: A used-car lot on the edge of an Indian city in the morning, rows of hatchbacks and sedans with price cards on their windscreens. In the foreground, a careful buyer in his early 30s, office shirt and a backpack, stands beside a silver hatchback with its bonnet open, while the friendly lot owner in a polo shirt holds out the papers. Four rounded callout bubbles connect to different parts of the car with thin lines: from the dusty tyres, a bubble showing a small map of city roads and highways it was driven on; from the open engine bay, a bubble with a cut-away engine and a size badge; from the glovebox, a bubble showing a stamped service booklet with tuning notes; from the driver seat, a bubble showing a different driver behind the wheel each day, one cautious and one fast. The buyer holds a short checklist of his daily commute, a short route between home and office, and compares it with the bubbles. In the background, a mechanic friend crouches to look under the car with a torch, because not every detail is written in the papers. Clear bright light, thoughtful mood. Labels: "TRAINING DATA" on the map bubble, "ARCHITECTURE" on the engine bubble, "SAMPLING" on the driver bubble.

key: eating at every roadside stall
name: ch02_roadside_stalls_vs_home_cook
alt: Split illustration: a young man learning to cook by eating at countless roadside stalls, some making him sick, versus learning a few dishes properly from one excellent home cook.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same young man in his early 20s with a notebook in both halves. LEFT panel: a crowded night food street with dozens of stalls, smoke, neon and colourful carts; he hurries from stall to stall tasting pav bhaji, momos, chowmein, kebabs and golgappe, scribbling notes; his notebook is overflowing with many recipes, but one hand clutches his stomach and a small green queasy squiggle floats above his head, a stall in the background with flies over uncovered food. RIGHT panel: a calm home kitchen in daylight, a skilled grandmother in a cotton sari teaches him patiently at the stove, showing exactly how much tempering to add to dal; his notebook now has only three dishes written very neatly, each with a tick. At the bottom of the image, below the dividing line, a small bowl mixes a big scoop from the left and a small spoon from the right, showing real recipes blend both. Neon night tones on the left, soft warm daylight on the right. Labels: "WEB DATA" above the left panel, "CURATED DATA" above the right panel.

key: mostly English and a little Hindi
name: ch02_enquiry_clerk_languages
alt: A railway enquiry clerk answers an English question instantly but struggles slowly with a Marathi question, spelling each word out piece by piece.
scene: A railway station enquiry counter with a glass window and a speaking hole, viewed from inside the booth over the clerk's shoulder. The clerk, a man in his 40s in a light-blue uniform shirt, has learned most of his vocabulary from English posters pinned around his booth, with a few small Hindi posters among them and none in other languages. On the left of the window, a young businessman asks in English, and the clerk answers instantly with a single neat speech bubble; a small stopwatch icon shows a short time. On the right of the window, an elderly woman in a nine-yard sari asks her question in Marathi; the clerk frowns, flips through a thin phrasebook, and his answer appears as a long chain of small broken speech-bubble pieces, each one a fragment, with the train name slightly wrong, and a stopwatch icon showing five times longer. A queue grows behind her, people checking their watches. Fluorescent booth light, station bustle outside. Labels: "FAST" next to the English answer, "SLOW, MORE PIECES" next to the chain of fragments.

key: heart scan you go to a cardiologist
name: ch02_gp_vs_cardiologist
alt: A general physician in a colony clinic handles most everyday patients, while a cardiologist with walls of ECG strips reads a heart scan the GP never studied.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a small neighbourhood clinic with a green curtain, a general physician in her 50s with a stethoscope and a white coat over a sari sees a steady line of patients: a child with a cough, a man with a bandaged hand, a woman with a fever; a large tally board on the wall shows most of the colony's visits handled here, and her shelf holds general medicine books on many topics. RIGHT panel: a specialist heart clinic with a big monitor showing a heart scan, and the cardiologist, a focused man in his 40s with rimless glasses, studies an ECG strip held up to the light; behind him, an entire wall is covered floor to ceiling with thousands of filed ECG strips, his vast specialised experience. In the left panel, a thought bubble above the general physician shows a confident face trying to read a heart scan with a question mark, hinting that a general model may attempt the specialist task anyway. Clean clinic lighting on both sides. Labels: "GENERAL MODEL" above the left panel, "SPECIALIST" above the right panel.

key: keep the novel open and flip
name: ch02_summary_vs_open_novel
alt: Split illustration: a student writing an exam from a friend's one-paragraph summary of a novel, versus a student with the whole novel open flipping to any page while answering.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, two students at exam desks. LEFT panel: a college student in a hoodie stares at a single small chit of paper with one short paragraph on it, handed over by a friend who is walking away holding a thick novel under his arm; a thought bubble above the student is full of question marks as he tries to answer detailed questions about chapter twelve, his answer sheet mostly blank. RIGHT panel: a second student in a kurta has the same thick novel open on her desk, with many coloured bookmarks sticking out of the pages; small curved arrows run from each question on her paper to a different bookmarked page, and she writes her answer word by word with a steady pen. An inset at the top right shows her earlier skimming the whole book at once with all pages fanned out in parallel, sticking bookmarks in. Soft reading-room light, calm determined mood on the right, worried mood on the left. Labels: "SEQ2SEQ" above the left panel, "TRANSFORMER" above the right panel, "PREFILL" beside the skimming inset.

key: A tiffin factory line. The embedding
name: ch02_tiffin_factory_transformer
alt: A tiffin factory line where trays get seat numbers, pass through identical stations each with an attention worker and a cooking worker, and reach a packing counter.
scene: A long industrial kitchen seen from the side, with a conveyor belt running left to right carrying a row of steel tiffin trays. At the far LEFT, an entry desk where a worker in a hairnet places each order chit onto a tray and stamps a seat number on it, 1, 2, 3, 4, in order. Then the belt passes through a series of identical stations, at least three visible with more fading into the distance, each station framed the same way. At every station stand two workers in white aprons: the first worker leans across and looks at all the other trays on the belt, with dotted sight-lines fanning out from her eyes to every tray, figuring out what this tray needs; the second worker beside her stirs a pot and adds a ladle of curry into the tray based on what the first worker tells him. Each tray becomes a little more complete after every station. At the far RIGHT, a packing counter where a supervisor with a clipboard looks at the finished tray and picks one dish card from a rack of many to ship. Bright factory lighting, orderly rhythmic mood. Labels: "POSITION" on the entry desk, "ATTENTION" above the first worker, "MLP" above the second worker.

key: the QWERTY keyboard or the Indian
name: ch02_broad_gauge_ecosystem_lockin
alt: A broad-gauge railway surrounded by an ecosystem of workshops, depots and trained crews, while a fancy new track design sits alone on paper, and a train mixes in a few sleek new coaches.
scene: A wide aerial view of a busy Indian railway junction built around one broad-gauge track. Around the track, a whole ecosystem: a locomotive workshop with cranes, a coach depot with spare wheels sized exactly for this gauge, a training school with crews in uniform, signal cabins and maintenance gangs, all connected to the track by small arrows. In the lower left corner, an engineer in a short-sleeved shirt stands at a drafting table holding a blueprint of a clever new track design with a different width; it looks good on paper, but no workshop, depot or crew is connected to it, and it sits alone in an empty field. On the main track, a long ordinary passenger train runs past, and in its middle a few sleek modern streamlined coaches are coupled in among the older coaches, showing a mix of new and old. An inset at the top right shows a keyboard with its familiar letter layout, a hand typing on it confidently. Clear afternoon light, a feeling of a big established system. Labels: "TRANSFORMER" on the broad-gauge track, "BETTER ON PAPER" on the blueprint, "HYBRID" above the mixed coaches.

key: the total kilometres of a trip
name: ch02_flops_road_trip
alt: A road trip from Delhi to Mumbai showing distance as total work, a car's top speed as compute speed, and traffic as utilisation.
scene: A long highway map-like illustration stretching from left to right, with a city skyline marked as the start on the left and a coastal city skyline with the sea as the end on the right; a sign at the start reads "1,400 km". A small hatchback travels along the highway, driven by a man in his 30s with sunglasses. Below the car, a large speedometer inset shows the needle's maximum marked in red at the top of the dial, while the actual needle points around the middle. The highway itself is divided into stretches: some segments are jammed with trucks, buses and tractors, slowing the car, while one segment is an almost empty expressway where the car speeds freely. A thin bar along the bottom of the image shows how much of the trip was spent at top speed, about half filled. At the far right corner, a small inset shows the same 1,400 km trip split among many tiny cars driving side by side on parallel lanes, all arriving sooner. Bright daytime light, travel mood. Labels: "FLOPS" on the distance sign, "FLOP/S" on the speedometer, "UTILIZATION" on the bottom bar.

key: done things one way for 20 years
name: ch02_senior_habit_vs_new_rule
alt: A veteran clerk and a new intern are told a strange new rule for filling a form; the intern follows it while the veteran slips back into his old habit.
scene: A government office with wooden desks and stacks of files, viewed from the front. A supervisor in a sari stands at a whiteboard where she has written an odd new instruction with an example showing a date written in reverse order. At two desks facing her sit two clerks filling the same form. On the left, a senior clerk in his late 50s with grey hair, thick spectacles and a sleeveless sweater writes automatically, a thought bubble above him full of twenty years of identical stamped forms stacked like a tower; his pen writes the date the usual way and a small red cross appears on his form. On the right, a young intern in her early 20s with a lanyard reads the whiteboard carefully and writes the date in reverse as instructed; a small green tick appears on her form. On the wall, a framed long-service certificate hangs above the senior clerk's desk. The supervisor looks mildly surprised, holding a cup of tea. Warm afternoon light, gentle and slightly humorous mood. Labels: "HABIT" above the senior clerk, "NEW RULE" on the whiteboard.

key: a tiny syllabus revised ten times
name: ch02_chinchilla_exam_hours
alt: Three students with the same fixed study hours: one skims a huge syllabus once, one revises a tiny syllabus ten times, and one balances syllabus size with practice.
scene: A three-panel strip of three students preparing for the same exam, each with an identical hourglass on the desk showing the same fixed amount of time. LEFT panel: a boy in a hoodie sits behind a towering pile of thick textbooks that reaches the ceiling, skimming one page at a time with a panicked face; most books are untouched and the hourglass is almost empty. MIDDLE panel: a girl in a school pinafore holds one thin booklet, its pages dog-eared and worn from being read again and again; ten tally marks are chalked on a slate beside her, and she looks bored, staring out of the window. RIGHT panel: a third student in a kurta has a balanced, medium stack of books and a matching stack of practice worksheets beside it, roughly twenty sheets for every book, all neatly ticked; she looks calm and confident. Below the three panels, a simple balance scale shows a small brain icon on one pan and a pile of practice sheets on the other, level. Warm study-lamp light in all three rooms. Labels: "TOO BIG" above the left panel, "TOO SMALL" above the middle panel, "BALANCED" above the right panel.

key: testing a new biryani recipe
name: ch02_biryani_scaling_test
alt: A caterer tests a biryani recipe in small, medium and large pots at home, plots how cooking time changes with size, and extrapolates to a huge wedding degh.
scene: A caterer's home kitchen, viewed from the side, that opens through a doorway onto a wedding venue in the far background. The caterer, a stout man in his 50s with a white cap, a moustache and an apron, stands at a counter with three test pots in a row from small to large: a small pressure cooker, a medium steel pot and a larger aluminium handi, each with a small tag showing its size and a timer beside it. He tastes from the smallest with a spoon. On the wall above, a chalkboard has a hand-drawn graph with three dots for the three pots and a dashed line extended far to the right toward a big empty circle. Through the doorway in the background, a wedding tent glows with string lights, and a giant copper degh, big enough for a person to sit in, sits on a firewood stove waiting, with stacks of plates for two thousand guests. An inset bubble near the giant degh shows a cut-away of its bottom with a dark burnt layer, a problem that only appears at the big size. Warm evening light, careful planning mood. Labels: "SMALL TESTS" over the three pots, "EXTRAPOLATE" along the dashed line, "SURPRISE AT SCALE" on the burnt-bottom inset.

key: every new building just drilled
name: ch02_groundwater_data_running_out
alt: A city where every new building drills a borewell, the water table is dropping, some plots are fenced off, some wells get recycled water, and the power grid is strained.
scene: A cut-away cross-section of a growing Indian city, showing buildings above ground and soil layers below. Above ground, a row of apartment blocks, each newer one with a borewell rig drilling straight down; old buildings on the left have short pipes, new ones on the right have very long pipes. Below ground, a blue water layer is visible, and a dashed line with a down arrow shows the water table dropping lower toward the right. Several plots on the surface have new tall fences with padlocks and signs, and the pipes under those plots are blocked off. Two wells on the far right have a pipe feeding in from a recycling plant, with slightly murky grey water mixing into the clean blue. Behind the buildings, an electricity pylon line connects to a substation where a meter needle is pressed against the red zone and a worried lineman looks up at buzzing wires. In one corner, a monsoon cloud drips a few thin drops, far too little to refill the water quickly. Hazy hot afternoon light, a sense of pressure on resources. Labels: "DATA RUNNING OUT" by the dropping water table, "FENCED OFF" on a fence, "AI-GENERATED" on the recycled water pipe.

key: SFT is the apprenticeship
name: ch02_graduate_apprentice_feedback
alt: A three-step strip: a student reads every book in a library, then apprentices with a senior at a service desk, then is polished by months of customer feedback cards.
scene: A three-step horizontal strip showing one young woman's journey, linked by arrows, with the first step drawn widest. STEP ONE, the widest: a huge library hall with endless shelves; the student, about 22 with a cloth bag and spectacles, sits surrounded by towers of books she has read, a glowing head showing she has absorbed huge knowledge but she has never worked. STEP TWO: a customer service desk in an office; a senior colleague, a kind woman in her 40s with a headset, stands beside her and demonstrates exactly how to answer a visiting customer, the trainee copying her words on a notepad. STEP THREE: the same desk months later, the trainee now confident and polished, while a box on the desk fills with small feedback cards; two cards are held up side by side, one with a smiley and one with a frown, showing that customers pick which reply was better. A small bar under each step shows how much effort each step took: a huge bar under step one and tiny bars under steps two and three. Clean daylight throughout, encouraging mood. Labels: "PRE-TRAINING" under step one, "SFT" under step two, "PREFERENCE" under step three.

key: 13,000 recorded calls handled
name: ch02_call_centre_trainee_recordings
alt: A call-centre trainee listens to thousands of recorded calls handled by the best senior agents, learning how to respond rather than new product facts.
scene: A call-centre training room with rows of desks and headsets, viewed from behind a trainee. The trainee, a young man in his early 20s with a neat haircut and an ID card, wears headphones and sits in front of a screen listing a very long column of recorded calls. Behind his screen, on a wall-sized rack, thousands of labelled audio cassettes or audio files are stacked floor to ceiling, each tagged with a small star to show it was handled by one of the best senior agents. A sound-wave line runs from the rack into his headphones, and in a thought bubble above his head appear only polite phrases and response patterns, not product catalogues. In the background, behind a glass partition, two senior agents in smart clothes carefully record a new model answer into a microphone, with a small coin stack beside them showing that each answer is costly expert work. On the trainee's desk, a product manual sits closed and untouched. Calm office lighting, focused learning mood. Labels: "HOW TO RESPOND" in the thought bubble, "EXPERT ANSWERS" on the wall rack.

key: radio jockey) on a city FM station
name: ch02_radio_jockey_judgement
alt: A new radio jockey at a city FM station speaks smoothly into the microphone while the station manager behind the glass teaches judgement about what not to say.
scene: A small FM radio studio with foam-covered walls, a big microphone on an arm and an ON AIR light glowing red. At the console sits a new radio jockey, an energetic young woman in her mid-20s with headphones and a bright scarf, speaking smoothly with a lively smile. Behind a glass window in the control room, the station manager, a calm man in his 40s with a beard and a kurta, holds up a series of hand-drawn cue cards to guide her: one with a crossed-out angry face, one with a crossed-out lock pick, one with a cautious yellow sign showing a temple and a parliament dome, and one with a yawning face crossed out, showing she must not be boring either. On the wall behind her, small framed listener maps show several different cities with differently coloured audiences. A listener-feedback box on the desk overflows with notes, and a rulebook lies open beside it with many pages crossed out and rewritten, because no single rulebook fits every city. Warm studio light with the red on-air glow, lively but careful mood. Labels: "ON AIR" on the red light, "JUDGEMENT" above the manager's cue cards.

key: Judging a school singing competition
name: ch02_singing_contest_pairwise
alt: Split illustration: judges giving inconsistent scores out of ten to a singer, versus judges simply picking which of two singers was better, building a ranking ladder.
scene: A school auditorium with a small stage, bunting and a harmonium. Split down the middle by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: one schoolgirl in a uniform sings on stage, and below three judges at a table each hold up a score card with a different number, 7, 5 and 9; the judges look at each other's cards in confusion. RIGHT panel: two schoolchildren, a boy and a girl, stand side by side on stage after singing, and the three judges each simply point toward the girl, with a tick card; beside the stage, a tall ladder chart on an easel shows many singers' photos placed on rungs, with arrows showing them moving up or down after each head-to-head result, like a chess rating ladder. Parents in the audience clap; a teacher holds a microphone; a student volunteer at the side records each head-to-head result on a long sheet of paper, one row per pair, which feeds the ladder. Warm stage lights and a festive school atmosphere. Labels: "SCORE OUT OF 10" above the left panel, "A OR B?" above the right panel, "RATING" on the ladder chart.

key: plays 8 balls and the selector films
name: ch02_cricket_coach_vs_best_of_n
alt: Split illustration: a coach improving a batter's technique over time, versus a selector filming eight balls in the nets and keeping only the best shot for the highlight reel.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves at a cricket ground's practice nets. LEFT panel: an experienced coach in a tracksuit and cap adjusts a young batter's elbow and stance, with a sequence of three faint ghosted versions of the batter behind him showing his technique steadily improving over weeks, the shots getting cleaner; a small calendar with crossed-off days sits on a kitbag. RIGHT panel: the same batter faces a bowling machine, and eight balls are shown as eight small film frames in a strip along the top: some edges, a miss, a block and one perfect cover drive; a selector with sunglasses and a video camera on a tripod circles only the perfect shot frame and drops it into a box labelled for the highlight reel, while the batter himself has not changed. Both panels share a coach's clipboard on the ground between them. Bright morning sunlight, green turf and white nets. Labels: "CHANGE THE PLAYER" above the left panel, "PICK THE BEST" above the right panel.

key: scores each item in his head
name: ch02_chaat_stall_softmax
alt: A chaat vendor's mental scores for pani puri, bhel, sev puri and dahi puri turn into recommendation shares, shown as a greedy choice versus a sampled choice.
scene: A busy evening chaat stall under a string of bulbs, viewed from the customers' side. The vendor, a cheerful man in his 40s with a vest, a towel on his shoulder and a big steel plate of puris, stands behind his cart with four dishes displayed in front: pani puri, bhel, sev puri and dahi puri. A large thought bubble above his head shows a little hand-written scoreboard beside each dish with plus and minus scores. From the thought bubble, a funnel converts the scores into a pie chart where pani puri has the biggest slice, bhel a medium slice and the others thin slivers. Below the cart, two customer scenes appear side by side: on the left, a customer is handed pani puri again with a resigned face, a calendar showing every day the same; on the right, a regular gets bhel this time and smiles in pleasant surprise, while a small spinning wheel shaped like the pie chart is shown next to the vendor's hand. Warm bulb light, lively street mood with traffic blur behind. Labels: "SCORES" in the thought bubble, "GREEDY" over the left customer, "SAMPLING" over the right customer.

key: Picking a restaurant with friends
name: ch02_friends_pick_restaurant_topk_topp
alt: Friends choosing a restaurant from a ranked list, with a fixed cut after the top five, a cut once most of the group's wishes are covered, and a minimum-rating cut.
scene: A group of five friends in their 20s sit on a low wall outside a college gate in the evening, heads together over one phone; a large ranked list of restaurants floats above them like a tall vertical scoreboard, each row a little restaurant icon with a bar showing how much the group wants it. Three different cutting tools act on this list, shown side by side as three small versions of the same list. FIRST list: a pair of scissors cuts straight across after exactly the fifth row, even though the sixth row's bar is almost as long. SECOND list: for a breakfast craving, two rows of small South Indian tiffin places are filled up to a marked line and the scissors cut there, very early; beside it a second version for dinner shows the scissors far down the list because many places share the wishes. THIRD list: a horizontal dotted floor line rejects every row whose bar is below a minimum. Below the lists, a small hand draws one restaurant from the remaining rows like pulling a chit from a bowl. Warm street light, friendly debating mood. Labels: "TOP-K" above the first list, "TOP-P" above the second list, "MIN-P" above the third list.

key: A TV news anchor with a hard time limit
name: ch02_news_anchor_cutoff
alt: Split illustration: a field reporter cut off mid-sentence while reading a phone number when a hard time limit hits, versus a reporter ending cleanly with a cue phrase.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a TV news studio with an anchor at a desk and a large screen behind her showing a live field reporter. LEFT panel: the studio clock on the wall hits zero with a red flash; on the big screen, a reporter in a rain jacket standing on a flooded street is frozen mid-sentence, his speech bubble chopped by a jagged cut that slices a helpline phone number in half so only the first few digits remain; a viewer at home in the corner inset holds a pen, puzzled, unable to write the number. The anchor looks startled and a producer behind the camera slaps his forehead. RIGHT panel: the same reporter finishes his sentence and the bubble ends with a clear closing phrase in quotes, "back to the studio", and the anchor smoothly turns to the next story with a calm smile; the studio clock shows a few seconds still left. A teleprompter and two camera operators frame the scene. Cool blue studio light with bright red on the left clock. Labels: "HARD LIMIT" above the left panel, "STOP WORD" above the right panel.

key: asks three colleagues to read the answer
name: ch02_examiner_majority_vote
alt: A paper-checker unsure of a student's handwriting asks three colleagues to read it and goes with the majority, while a recruiter in the next room interviews five candidates to hire the best.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a board exam evaluation room with piles of answer books; a middle-aged examiner in spectacles holds up an answer sheet with one smudged handwritten word circled, and three colleagues lean in around her, each with a small speech bubble giving their reading; two bubbles agree and are ticked, one differs, and she writes the majority reading on her mark sheet. RIGHT panel: an office meeting room where a recruiter, a woman in her 30s in a blazer, sits across from a row of five candidate chairs; five candidates take turns, each shown faintly in sequence, and she holds a score sheet with five rows, circling the best.
