In the corner of the right panel, a much longer row of candidates trails out of the door into the corridor, and the very last one in line wears a sly grin and a fake medal, hinting that interviewing too many finds someone good at fooling the interviewer. Fluorescent office light, ordinary working mood. Labels: "MAJORITY VOTE" above the left panel, "BEST OF N" above the right panel.

key: a form with one box per letter
name: ch02_government_form_five_fixes
alt: Five ways to get a government form filled correctly: instructions, a clerk fixing slips, handing out fresh forms, a box-per-letter form with dropdowns, and training the applicant.
scene: A government office counter shown as a horizontal strip of five small scenes side by side, all featuring the same applicant, a nervous young man in a checked shirt, and the same form. SCENE ONE: a clerk points at a printed notice telling applicants to write in capitals inside the boxes. SCENE TWO: a second clerk with a red pen quietly fixes a small slip on a submitted form, adding a missing letter. SCENE THREE: the applicant sits with a pile of crumpled forms beside him as a clerk hands him one fresh form after another until one is filled right. SCENE FOUR: a specially designed form with one small square box per letter and a dropdown arrow for the state field, making wrong entries physically impossible; the applicant fills it easily. SCENE FIVE: the applicant attends a short training session with a teacher at a blackboard and later fills the form perfectly by himself. Above the whole strip, a thin banner unites them. Neutral office lighting, ceiling fans and wooden counters. Labels: "PROMPTING" above scene one, "TEST TIME COMPUTE" above scene three, "CONSTRAINED SAMPLING" above scene four.

key: always forgets the full stop
name: ch02_typist_full_stop_proofread
alt: An office manager checks every typed letter and adds the full stop the typist always forgets before posting, rather than retraining the typist.
scene: A small typing pool in an old office, viewed from the side. On the left, a typist in his 30s with oiled hair and a short-sleeved shirt types rapidly on a typewriter, and a stack of finished letters grows on his desk; on each letter, an inset magnifier shows the last sentence ending without its full stop. In the middle, a conveyor-like wire tray carries the letters to the right. On the right, the office manager, a calm woman in her 50s with reading glasses on a chain, stands at a small table beside a post-box slot, and with a fountain pen she quickly adds the missing dot at the end of each letter before sliding it into an envelope. A small poster about a typing course is pinned on the wall behind the typist, ignored, showing that retraining was not needed. In the far corner, a single letter in the tray is completely different, addressed to the wrong person, and the manager's pen hovers over it uselessly, a hint that a checker cannot fix every error. Soft afternoon light through blinds, orderly mood. Labels: "POST-PROCESSING" above the manager, "MISSING DOT" on the magnifier inset.

key: pen with a three-button stamp
name: ch02_writer_sorting_clerk_stamp
alt: A writer working as a sorting clerk scribbles labels on letters and sometimes writes something else, versus a three-button stamp that can only print urgent, normal or spam.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, inside a post office sorting room with pigeonholes on the wall. LEFT panel: a brilliant writer in her 30s in a shawl, more used to writing novels, sits at a sorting table and hand-writes a label on each envelope with a fountain pen; most labels read the expected words, but one envelope has a long poetic sentence scribbled across it and she looks a little embarrassed, a pile of practice envelopes beside her showing weeks of training. RIGHT panel: the same writer at the same table, but her pen has been replaced by a chunky three-button stamp machine bolted to the desk; each button prints one fixed word onto the envelope, and the stamped envelopes slide neatly into three bins. One envelope in the middle bin is clearly marked urgent by its red border, showing that the stamp makes the format certain but not the judgement correct. Warm sorting-room light, steady and practical mood. Labels: "FINETUNED PEN" above the left panel, "CLASSIFIER HEAD" above the right panel, "NORMAL" on the middle bin.

key: getting two different answers from two
name: ch02_bank_helpline_two_answers
alt: A customer calls a bank helpline twice with the same question and gets two different answers from two agents, while the bank tries scripts and an FAQ binder.
scene: A split-level illustration. UPPER area: a man in his 40s in a home kurta sits on his sofa holding a phone to his ear twice, shown as two side-by-side moments; above each moment, a speech bubble shows the same question with a rupee symbol and a calendar. LOWER area: a cut-away of a bank's call centre with rows of agents in headsets. In the first call, a young male agent answers with a bubble showing one answer; in the second call, a young female agent two seats away answers with a bubble showing a different answer. Two thin phone-line wires lead from the customer's two moments to the two different agents, routed by a small spinning dice on a switchboard between them. On the agents' desks, the bank's fixes are visible: a printed script clipped to each monitor and a thick ring-bound FAQ binder of approved answers on a shared shelf. A third tiny bubble shows the customer rephrasing slightly and the line jumping to yet another agent. Cool office light below, warm home light above. Labels: "SAME QUESTION" over the customer, "DIFFERENT ANSWERS" over the agents, "SCRIPT AND FAQ" by the binder.

key: a nervous student in a viva
name: ch02_viva_bluff_coaching_answers
alt: Split illustration: a nervous student in a viva building a story around one wrong date, and a coaching class drilling students to memorise confident model answers they do not understand.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a college viva room with a long table, two stern examiners in formal clothes and a nervous student in a white shirt and tie, sweating, gesturing as he talks; his first speech bubble contains a small wrong date, and from it a chain of further bubbles grows like a tower of cards, each one building on the wrong date to stay consistent, wobbling dangerously; one examiner raises an eyebrow and taps a history book. RIGHT panel: a crowded coaching class with a banner of toppers on the wall; a loud teacher with a pointer makes rows of students recite model answers from a printed sheet packed with facts; the students' thought bubbles are empty or show question marks, yet they speak with big confident mouths, and a small gold star sticker is handed to the loudest speaker, showing that confidence is what gets rewarded. Tense warm light on the left, harsh tube light on the right. Labels: "SELF-DELUSION" above the left panel, "MISMATCHED KNOWLEDGE" above the right panel.

key: the train change at Dadar
name: ch03_dabbawala_route_checkpoints
alt: A map of a new tiffin delivery route with checkers posted at the known trouble spots, a train change and a building with no lift, counting late and wrong deliveries every day.
scene: A bird's-eye illustrated map of a tiffin delivery route through a busy Indian city, drawn like a board game path from homes on the left to office towers on the right. Along the path, dabbawalas in white caps carry crates on bicycles, on a crowded suburban train and on foot. Two trouble spots are highlighted with warning circles: a busy station platform where crates are transferred between trains, with one crate dropped and tiffins rolling, and a tall old building with an out-of-order lift sign where a dabbawala sweats up the stairs. At each trouble spot stands a checker, a young woman with a clipboard and a whistle, ticking boxes. At the end of the route, a wall chart in a small office shows a daily tally of late and wrong deliveries, with a supervisor in spectacles studying it. In the corner, two faded figures represent the methods not trusted: a cousin whispering into someone's ear with a thumbs up, and a man watching just one delivery through binoculars and shrugging. Bright morning light, organised and watchful mood. Labels: "CHECKPOINT" at the station platform, "COUNT FAILURES" above the wall chart.

key: students who keep scoring 100/100
name: ch03_board_papers_saturation
alt: A board office writes ever harder question papers because students keep scoring full marks on the old one, while an expert examiner reads a long open-ended essay.
scene: An exam board office shown in two zones. LEFT zone: a notice board shows rows of students' report cards, all stamped with full marks on the same old question paper, the paper itself pinned at the top looking worn and faded; a group of grinning students holds up their perfect scorecards. CENTRE: a worried board official in a grey safari suit sits at a desk writing a new paper, and behind him a staircase of stacked question papers rises upward, each one thicker and harder than the last, with the newest at the top still being written. RIGHT zone: an expert examiner, an older woman with a shawl and reading glasses, sits at a separate desk carefully reading a long handwritten essay answer, a pencil in hand making margin notes, with a stack of many such essays behind her, each different. In the foreground, a closed black box with a question mark on it sits beside the students, representing not knowing how they studied. Daylight office tones, slightly hectic mood. Labels: "SATURATED" across the old paper, "HARDER PAPERS" along the staircase, "OPEN-ENDED" above the examiner.

key: only one train stops each day
name: ch03_station_announcement_entropy
alt: Split illustration: an announcement at a tiny station where only one train stops tells nobody anything new, versus an announcement at a huge terminus where it could be any of dozens of trains.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a tiny rural railway station with a single platform, a neem tree, a goat and a lone tea stall; a loudspeaker on a pole crackles an announcement, and the only two waiting passengers, a farmer and his wife with a bundle, barely look up, already picking up their luggage because only one train ever stops here; a timetable board shows a single row. RIGHT panel: a gigantic busy terminus with many platforms, a huge iron roof and a giant departure board with dozens of rows; the loudspeaker makes an announcement and hundreds of passengers turn their heads at once with alert faces, some starting to run toward one platform, because it could have been any of many trains. A large number sign hangs over the announced platform, and porters in red shirts lift luggage onto their heads, ready to dash. Quiet golden evening light on the left, bustling bright light on the right. Labels: "LOW ENTROPY" above the left panel, "HIGH ENTROPY" above the right panel.

key: stocks up based on what he thinks
name: ch03_kirana_stock_kl_waste
alt: A kirana shop owner stocks by his own beliefs while real customer demand differs, and the waste is split into unavoidable randomness and extra waste from wrong beliefs.
scene: Inside a narrow kirana shop with floor-to-ceiling shelves, viewed from the counter. The owner, a man in his 50s with a white vest, reading glasses on his nose and a ledger, has stocked his shelves according to a thought bubble above his head showing his beliefs: a huge pile of charcoal sacks and only a few packets of tea. In front of the counter, the real customers queue, each holding a small speech bubble with what they want: almost all want tea and milk, almost none want charcoal. Below the shelves, two separate heaps of wasted goods lie on the floor: a small heap of a few expired items that would happen anyway because demand wobbles day to day, drawn with a dice icon, and a much bigger heap of unsold charcoal sacks caused by his wrong belief, drawn with a crossed-out thought bubble icon. A simple stacked bar on the wall adds the two heaps together into total waste. Warm tube-light glow, everyday shop mood. Labels: "RANDOMNESS" on the small heap, "WRONG BELIEFS" on the big heap, "TOTAL WASTE" on the stacked bar.

key: A tabla teacher listening to a student
name: ch03_tabla_teacher_perplexity
alt: A tabla teacher listens to three students: one playing a memorised syllabus piece with no surprise, one banging randomly, and one playing a new but sensible composition.
scene: A music classroom with a carpet, a harmonium and framed portraits of anonymous musicians on the wall. An elderly tabla teacher with a white beard and a shawl sits cross-legged at the front, eyes half closed, listening intently. Facing him, three students each play a pair of tabla, shown left to right. LEFT: a teenage boy plays smoothly from a printed syllabus sheet that has a small stamp suggesting it was the exam piece; the teacher's reaction meter above him barely moves, a flat calm line, and the teacher looks almost too relaxed. MIDDLE: a small boy bangs wildly, both hands flying, and the meter above him spikes chaotically while the teacher winces and covers one ear. RIGHT: a girl in a salwar suit plays a new composition she made, and the meter shows small, pleasant wiggles, a little surprise but in the right rhythm; the teacher raises an eyebrow with interest. Warm late-afternoon light through a window, cultural and gentle mood. Labels: "MEMORISED" above the left student, "GIBBERISH" above the middle student, "NEW BUT SENSIBLE" above the right student.

key: commentator predicting each ball
name: ch03_commentator_gasp_level
alt: A cricket commentator predicts each ball of an over correctly until one unexpected switch-hit makes him gasp, and a small meter averages his surprise across the over.
scene: A commentary box high above a cricket stadium, glass windows overlooking the green field. A commentator in his 50s in a blazer and headset leans toward the microphone. Along the bottom of the image, a strip of six panels shows the six balls of an over as seen through the window, each with a small prediction bubble from the commentator above it: ball one a defensive push, ball two a leave outside off, ball three a single, ball four a defence; in each case a tick shows the prediction matched and his face is calm. Ball five shows the batter suddenly switching stance and hitting a reverse shot for six, and the commentator's face in that panel is a huge gasp, eyes wide, hands on head, his prediction bubble crossed out. Ball six returns to calm. Above the strip, a meter like a dial shows his average surprise across the over, and the needle has been pushed noticeably higher by the single big gasp. A scorecard and a cup of tea sit on the commentary desk. Bright stadium daylight, excited mood. Labels: "PREDICTION" on the first bubble, "SURPRISE" by the gasp panel, "PERPLEXITY" on the meter.

key: flip every switch and check
name: ch03_electrician_switch_tests
alt: An inspector tests an electrician's work by flipping every switch, and a counter shows a room passing if any of three attempts works.
scene: A newly wired apartment shown as a cut-away floor plan with three rooms side by side, viewed from slightly above. In each room, an inspector in a cap with a clipboard flips the wall switches one by one, and above each switch the light bulb or ceiling fan responds: most glow or spin with a green tick, one bulb in the kitchen stays dark with a red cross. The electrician, a young man in a blue work shirt with a tool belt and a coil of wire, waits at the door holding a rolled-up wiring diagram that nobody reads. Beside each room, a small row of three attempt boxes shows the electrician's tries: in the bedroom, the first try failed and the second worked; in the kitchen all three failed. A scoreboard at the right shows rooms counted as done if any attempt worked. A small note at the bottom right shows one real house with a single attempt per room, drawn more seriously. Fresh paint tins and a ladder stand in a corner. Bright clean daylight, practical mood. Labels: "UNIT TESTS" above the switches, "PASS@3" on the scoreboard.

key: English translation of a Hindi sentence
name: ch03_translation_four_checks
alt: A student's translation is checked four ways: word-for-word against a key, counting shared words, comparing meaning, and asking a teacher.
scene: A classroom desk viewed from above, with a student's notebook in the centre showing one handwritten English sentence translated from a Hindi sentence written above it. Around the notebook, four checking stations are arranged in four corners. TOP LEFT: a ruler laid under the student's sentence and the answer key, aligning word by word, with a strict red cross because one word differs. TOP RIGHT: a magnifying glass and a counter counting how many words from the key appear in the student's sentence, a small tally of matching words. BOTTOM LEFT: two thought bubbles, one from the key sentence and one from the student's, both showing the same simple picture of a boy giving a mango to his grandmother, joined by an equals sign. BOTTOM RIGHT: a kind teacher in a cardigan reads the sentence and nods, giving a tick. On the edge of the desk, an answer key booklet shows only one or two printed versions. Soft classroom light, studious mood. Labels: "EXACT MATCH" at top left, "SEMANTIC" at bottom left, "EVALUATOR" at bottom right.

key: checking a payment reference number
name: ch03_payment_ref_vs_complaint_letter
alt: Split illustration: exact character matching works well for a payment reference number, but matching a complaint letter word for word against templates is absurd.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a close-up of a shopkeeper's phone screen beside a customer's phone, two long payment reference numbers lined up one above the other, every character matched by little vertical tick lines from end to end and a big green tick; the shopkeeper, a young man behind a counter of snacks, smiles and hands over the goods. RIGHT panel: a customer service office where a clerk in his 30s holds a long handwritten complaint letter from an elderly customer up beside three printed approved templates pinned to a board, trying to match it word by word with a ruler; red crosses cover almost every line, the clerk looks baffled, and the elderly customer waits angrily across the desk. A small inset at the bottom of the left panel shows a sneaky reference number containing the correct digits hidden inside a longer wrong number, accepted with a questionable tick. Bright shop light on the left, dull office light on the right. Labels: "EXACT MATCH WORKS" above the left panel, "EXACT MATCH FAILS" above the right panel.

key: marks answers by counting keywords
name: ch03_keyword_counting_teacher
alt: A teacher marks answers by counting textbook keywords, rewarding a student who copies keywords into a wrong sentence and penalising one who writes the right idea in her own words.
scene: A school staffroom with a long table and stacks of answer books. A teacher in his 40s with a pen behind his ear and a checked shirt marks with a highlighter, and beside him lies the open textbook answer with a few keywords circled. Two answer sheets lie in front of him. On the left sheet, a girl's neat handwriting explains the idea correctly in her own words, but none of the circled keywords appear, and the teacher gives it a low mark in red; a small photo-clip of the student shows her looking disappointed. On the right sheet, a boy's messy answer strings together all the circled keywords in a sentence that is clearly wrong, shown by a small illustration of a plant growing upside down, yet the teacher gives it high marks, and the boy's photo-clip shows a smug grin. On the textbook page itself, one keyword is printed with a small error mark, and faint lines carry that mistake into every sheet. Afternoon light through a window with a ceiling fan turning, ironic mood. Labels: "RIGHT IDEA, LOW MARKS" over the left sheet, "WRONG IDEA, HIGH MARKS" over the right sheet.

key: giving directions in Bengaluru
name: ch03_two_directions_same_route
alt: Two people give differently worded directions that trace the same route on a map, and the two directions appear as nearby arrows on a map of meanings.
scene: A city street corner in Bengaluru with a big shopping mall in the background, a coconut seller and two-wheelers passing. A lost young woman with a backpack and a phone stands in the middle. On her left, a college student in a T-shirt points and gives directions with a speech bubble showing a sketch of a left turn after a mall icon. On her right, an elderly man in a white shirt and a cap gives his directions with a speech bubble showing a different sketch, a turn toward a neighbourhood sign at a large building. Above them, a big folded paper city map floats open, and both people's routes are traced in two colours along exactly the same streets, overlapping. In the top right corner, a separate inset shows a simple compass-like diagram with two arrows starting from one point, one for each direction-giver's words, pointing almost the same way with a very small angle between them. The woman looks relieved. Warm late afternoon light, everyday city mood. Labels: "DIFFERENT WORDS" above the speech bubbles, "SAME MEANING" on the overlapping route, "SMALL ANGLE" on the inset.

key: Aadhaar for meaning. Every person
name: ch03_meaning_codes_on_map
alt: People, products and texts each get a number code placed as a dot on a map where similar things sit close together, and a photo and its description share nearby codes.
scene: A large wall-sized map pinned in a bright office, with no countries or roads, only soft coloured regions like neighbourhoods. A friendly clerk in her 30s in a lanyard and cotton saree stands at a desk issuing small ID-style cards, each card with a short number code and a small picture: a mango, a cricket bat, a recipe card, a pair of sandals, a short text slip about monsoon rain. A helper on a stepladder pins each card onto the map as a dot, and similar items cluster together: all the fruits in one corner, all the sports items in another, all the weather texts in a third. In the centre of the map, a single person's photo card and a handwritten card describing that person in words are pinned right next to each other, connected by a short line, showing that a picture and a description get nearby codes. A visitor stands at the map with a slip of description in hand, following an arrow straight to the matching photo. Bright office daylight, orderly and curious mood. Labels: "SIMILAR = CLOSE" in a corner of the map, "PHOTO" and "DESCRIPTION" beside the paired cards.

key: A cricket third umpire with replays
name: ch03_third_umpire_replays
alt: A third umpire reviews replays on screens and announces a decision with reasons on the big screen, while the crowd below argues noisily.
scene: A cricket stadium at night under floodlights, viewed from behind the third umpire's booth high in the pavilion. The third umpire, a calm man in his 50s in a neat blazer with a headset, sits before a bank of monitors showing slow-motion replays from several angles: a ball near the bat edge, a stump camera, a side view of the batter's foot. A printed rulebook lies open beside him, with a rubric of conditions ticked off one by one. Below, in the stands, a huge crowd shouts in every direction with mixed signs, some reading "OUT", some "NOT OUT", waving flags, arguing among themselves. On the giant stadium screen, the verdict appears with a short list of reasons drawn as small icons: a ball, an edge mark and a tick. In the corner, an inset shows three expert former players on a panel nodding in agreement with the umpire, as closely as they agree with one another. Bright white floodlights against a dark night sky, tense but authoritative mood. Labels: "RUBRIC" on the open rulebook, "VERDICT WITH REASONS" on the big screen.

key: giving them a checklist: education, job
name: ch03_rishta_rating_vs_checklist
alt: Split illustration: a relative vaguely rating a marriage proposal out of ten, versus a relative using a clear checklist with examples to give consistent, useful answers.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves set in a family living room with a sofa, a framed family photo and a plate of sweets. LEFT panel: an aunt in her 60s in a silk sari holds a biodata sheet with a candidate's photo, shrugs and says through a speech bubble "7, I guess", while a second relative beside her holding the same sheet says "5" and a third says "9"; the family member asking looks frustrated. RIGHT panel: the same aunt holds a neat printed checklist on a clipboard with four rows, each with small example icons, a graduation cap, a briefcase, a house with family figures and a map pin for distance; she fills each row with a tick or a short note, and the two other relatives beside her fill matching checklists that look almost identical. A small heart-shaped thought bubble above the aunt still shows her personal favourite, a hint that bias does not vanish. Warm homely lamp light, lightly humorous mood. Labels: "1 TO 10" above the left panel, "CHECKLIST" above the right panel.

key: re-mark the same answer sheet on Monday
name: ch03_examiner_monday_friday
alt: The same examiner marks the same answer sheet on Monday and Friday and gives different marks, then uses a marking scheme with sample answers to narrow the gap.
scene: A three-part illustration of the same examiner, a man in his 40s with a moustache, reading glasses and a pen, marking the same answer sheet. LEFT part: a Monday morning, a wall calendar showing Monday, sunlight streaming in, a fresh cup of tea; he writes 14 out of 20 on the sheet with a neutral face. MIDDLE part: a Friday evening, the calendar showing Friday, a dim tube light, a tall pile of finished answer books beside him, his tie loosened; he marks the same sheet 17 out of 20 with a tired, generous smile. RIGHT part: a new day with a printed marking scheme pinned beside him, showing three sample answers with marks next to them; now the two marks on his Monday and Friday sheets are drawn much closer together. But one line of the marking scheme has a small error mark, and faint lines show his marks following that error consistently. Changing light from bright to dim to neutral across the three parts. Labels: "MONDAY" above the left part, "FRIDAY" above the middle part, "MARKING SCHEME" on the pinned sheet.

key: Three restaurant apps rating
name: ch03_hygiene_ratings_not_comparable
alt: Three restaurant apps rate hygiene with stars, a pass or fail sticker and a yes or no tag, so the ratings are not comparable, and one app quietly changes its rules overnight.
scene: A restaurant entrance in an Indian city, viewed from the street, with a glass door covered in rating stickers. Beside the door, three oversized phones stand like signboards, each showing a different app's rating of the same restaurant's hygiene: the first shows four out of five stars, the second shows a round pass sticker, the third shows a small yes tag with a tick. A confused couple in their 30s stands on the pavement looking from one phone to the next, scratching their heads. Inside, visible through the glass, the kitchen is exactly the same throughout, a cook in a cap wiping a clean counter. In the top right corner, an inset night scene shows one app's office where a programmer quietly edits a rules document at midnight, and the next morning the star count on that phone drops by one star while the kitchen inside has not changed at all. Morning street light with a soft night-blue tint in the inset. Labels: "SAME WORD, DIFFERENT SCALES" above the three phones, "RULES CHANGED" on the inset.

key: every box of mithai is checked
name: ch03_mithai_checking_vs_spotcheck
alt: Split illustration: a sweet-shop owner checks every box before handing it over and the queue grows, versus spot-checking every tenth box while the queue moves fast.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves inside the same bright sweet shop with glass counters full of laddoos, barfi and jalebis. LEFT panel: the owner, a portly man in his 60s in a white kurta and a bandhgala jacket, opens every single box of mithai, inspects the pieces with a magnifying glass and closes it before handing it over; behind the counter a very long queue of customers stretches out of the door into the street, some looking at their watches, and a clock on the wall shows a lot of time passing. RIGHT panel: the same owner lets his assistant pack boxes quickly and only opens every tenth box, marked with a small number tag; the queue is short and moving, customers happy, but one box going out the door has a broken, crumbled laddoo visible through its window that slipped past the check. Trays of fresh sweets keep arriving from the kitchen behind. Warm golden lighting in both halves, festive marigold garlands around the door. Labels: "CHECK EVERY BOX" above the left panel, "SPOT-CHECK" above the right panel.

key: junior doctors see patients
name: ch03_hospital_junior_senior_review
alt: Junior doctors see a stream of patients during the day while a senior consultant reviews a small sample of their cases in the evening, and a radiologist reads only X-rays.
scene: A hospital shown as a cut-away building with two floors and a side room. GROUND floor, daytime: a large busy outpatient hall where three young junior doctors in white coats with stethoscopes quickly see a long line of patients, writing prescriptions on pads, a stack of case files growing beside them. UPPER floor, evening, with a window showing a sunset: a senior consultant, a grey-haired woman in her 60s with spectacles, sits at a desk and pulls out just a few files from the large stack, one of them marked with a red flag; she picks up her phone to step in. SIDE room: a radiologist in a dim room sits before a lightbox full of X-ray films, focused only on reading them, more expert at that one task than anyone else in the building. On the top of the building, an empty chair on the roof with a small question mark shows that the head of the hospital has nobody more senior to review her. Bright daylight downstairs, warm amber evening light upstairs. Labels: "CHEAP MODEL" on the ground floor, "STRONG JUDGE" by the consultant, "SPECIALISED JUDGE" by the radiologist.

key: IPL points table vs chess ratings
name: ch03_league_table_vs_chess_rating
alt: Split illustration: a cricket league points table where every team plays every other, versus a chess hall where many players meet random opponents and get a rating.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a cricket stadium scoreboard showing a neat points table with eight team rows, each with a coloured flag, columns for played, won and points; below it a small grid diagram shows every team connected to every other team with lines, each pair meeting twice; a cricket fan in a painted face points happily at the top team. RIGHT panel: a huge chess hall with many tables and many players of all ages, a schoolboy, an old man in a cap, a woman in a sari, a college student; random pairs face each other with lines connecting only some of the players, many never meeting; on the wall, a large rating board lists names with rating numbers going up or down with small arrows after each game. In one corner of the right panel, three players are connected in a small triangle of arrows, A beats B, B beats C, C beats A, a quiet hint that preferences can go round in circles. Bright stadium light on the left, quiet indoor light on the right. Labels: "ROUND ROBIN" above the left panel, "RATING" above the right panel.

key: Organisers use Swiss pairing instead
name: ch03_chess_swiss_pairing
alt: A school chess tournament where full round-robin with many players needs far too many games, so organisers pair players with similar scores instead.
scene: A school hall during a chess tournament, viewed from a balcony above. On the left wall, a giant round-robin chart drawn on chart paper shows a huge grid of every possible pairing among sixty players, so dense it looks like a wall of scribbles, and an organiser in a sports teacher's tracksuit stares at it in horror, holding his head. On the right, a second organiser, a calm teacher in her 40s with a whistle, uses a whiteboard with small magnetic name tags sorted into groups by current score; she moves tags to pair players with similar scores. On the hall floor below, pairs of students sit at boards: two players with three wins each play a close game, two players with one win each play another; a clear champion with a gold badge and an obvious beginner sit at distant tables with a crossed-out line between them, not paired again. Score sheets and water bottles on each table. Bright daylight through tall windows, focused tournament mood. Labels: "TOO MANY GAMES" above the round-robin chart, "SWISS PAIRING" above the whiteboard.

key: Judging the best biryani in the city
name: ch03_open_biryani_vote_vs_panel
alt: Split illustration: an open biryani vote where anyone walks in and many voters only tasted plain rice or troll, versus a small trained tasting panel judging carefully.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a big open food festival tent with a huge ballot box at the centre and a long noisy crowd dropping in voting slips; one man in a cap tastes only a spoonful of plain white rice before voting, a teenager with a mischievous grin votes for a dish marked with many red chillies just to cause trouble, and nobody's plate has the small bowl of raita that the restaurant serves alongside, a lone raita bowl sitting untouched on a side table. A vote counter shows a very large number. RIGHT panel: a quiet room with a long white table where three trained tasters in aprons, a chef, a food writer and an elderly cook, sit with score sheets, each carefully tasting a full biryani plate with raita, making notes; only a few plates are on the table and a small counter shows a much smaller number. Busy colourful festival light on the left, calm neutral light on the right. Labels: "OPEN VOTING" above the left panel, "TRAINED PANEL" above the right panel.

key: people preferred Ramesh over Suresh
name: ch03_driver_preference_vs_licence
alt: Two driver candidates after a test drive with people slightly preferring one, while the real question is whether either can safely drive the ghat road to the factory.
scene: A factory gate on the edge of town in the morning. In the foreground, two driver candidates in their 30s stand beside a company car, one in a light blue shirt and one in a cream shirt, both with neat moustaches and holding their licence booklets. A group of employees who took the test drive stands nearby, and a small tally board shows the votes split almost evenly between the two, with a narrow lead for the man in blue. The factory manager, a woman in her 40s in a formal kurta, looks past them with a doubtful expression, thinking: a thought bubble above her shows a dangerous winding ghat road with steep drops and hairpin bends leading up to the factory, and a second thought bubble shows a salary slip with a doubled number and a question mark. On the right side of the image, a separate small driving test track with cones and a sloped ramp waits, with an examiner holding a checklist, the real test still to be taken. Clear morning light, practical decision mood. Labels: "51% PREFERENCE" on the tally board, "ABSOLUTE TEST" above the test track.

key: kirana shop without deciding
name: ch04_kirana_goals_on_wall
alt: Split illustration: a kirana owner after six months unsure if the shop is doing well, versus an owner who wrote sales and spoilage targets on the wall before opening.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same small kirana shop with sacks of rice, jars of sweets and a steel counter in both halves. LEFT panel: six months after opening, a calendar with many pages torn off; the owner, a man in his 40s in a printed half-sleeve shirt, stands behind the counter scratching his head, surrounded by a jumble of unread receipts and a half-empty shelf, a big question mark floating above him, a few spoiled vegetables in a corner; he cannot tell if things are good or bad. RIGHT panel: the morning before opening day, the shutter half raised, the same owner standing on a stool and painting two clear targets on the wall above the counter with a brush: a daily sales goal with a rupee symbol and a spoilage limit with a small crate icon; on the counter below, a ruled notebook is ready with columns for sales, repeat customers and spoilage. His wife holds the paint tin and smiles. Dull uncertain light on the left, fresh hopeful morning light on the right. Labels: "NO GOAL" above the left panel, "SUCCESS DEFINED FIRST" above the right panel.

key: picking the right meaning of a road sign
name: ch04_licence_written_test_vs_junction
alt: Split illustration: a learner passing a road-sign multiple-choice test in a quiet office, versus the same learner frozen in heavy evening traffic at a chaotic city junction.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same young man in his early 20s with a backpack in both halves. LEFT panel: a quiet transport office test room with plastic chairs and a computer screen showing a road sign and four answer options; he confidently clicks the correct option and a large green tick appears, a printed pass slip sliding out of a printer. A small inset below shows the same question with an extra space added between options and his answer changing, with a nervous sweat drop. RIGHT panel: the same young man behind the wheel of a small car at a massive junction at six in the evening, a wall of honking buses, autos, bikes and trucks around him, a traffic signal that is not working, a policeman waving arms in the middle; he grips the steering wheel, frozen, eyes wide, the pass slip sticking uselessly out of his shirt pocket. Calm fluorescent light on the left, orange dusk and headlights on the right. Labels: "KNOWS THE SIGN" above the left panel, "CAN HE DRIVE?" above the right panel.

key: Twenty years ago you graded
name: ch04_child_essay_spelling_to_truth
alt: A parent once marked a child's essay for spelling and commas, and now marks the fluent grown-up child's essay for whether it is true and kind.
scene: A two-part illustration across time in the same family study with a wooden desk, a lamp and a bookshelf. LEFT part, faded warm tones, twenty years ago: a mother in her 30s in a cotton sari sits beside her eight-year-old son, marking his wobbly handwritten essay in a ruled notebook with a red pen, circling misspelled words and missing commas; the page is full of small red circles. RIGHT part, present day: the same mother, now in her 50s with grey streaks and reading glasses, sits beside her son, now a confident young man in his late 20s, who has written a fluent, beautifully formatted essay printed on clean paper. She no longer marks commas; instead, she writes two questions in the margin, one next to a small globe icon and one next to a small heart icon, and points at one sentence with a doubtful expression. The young man looks as confident about that sentence as about the rest. Golden sepia light on the left, crisp clean light on the right. Labels: "SPELLING" above the left part, "IS IT TRUE?" and "IS IT KIND?" beside the margin questions.

key: fact-checking desk at a newspaper
name: ch04_newspaper_fact_check_desk
alt: A newspaper fact-checking desk cuts an article into single claims, rewrites each to stand alone, looks each up and marks it true or false.
scene: A busy newspaper office at night with desks, monitors and piles of papers, viewed from above a long fact-checking desk. The process flows left to right. LEFT: an editor in her 40s with a pencil behind her ear takes a printed article and cuts it with a pair of scissors into separate strips, each strip carrying a single claim. MIDDLE: a young researcher in a sweater rewrites each strip on a fresh index card so it makes sense on its own, adding the missing name or date, with small arrows showing a pronoun replaced by a name. RIGHT: another researcher types each card into a search screen, with a stack of reference books and printouts beside him, and stamps each card with a tick or a cross; a small tray holds the stamped cards. In a small inset in the corner, a student's short précis is checked by a teacher only against the given passage on her desk, showing the narrower local check. Warm desk lamps against the dark office, diligent mood. Labels: "SPLIT CLAIMS" over the scissors, "SEARCH" over the screen, "VERDICT" over the stamped cards.

key: a cheap guard at the gate checks
name: ch04_society_guard_and_officer
alt: A housing society gate guard quickly checks every visitor and flags a few, whom a senior security officer then reviews closely.
scene: The entrance gate of an Indian housing society in the late afternoon, viewed from the road. A cabin beside the boom barrier holds a young security guard in a blue uniform and cap with a visitor register; a steady stream of visitors passes him: a delivery rider, a maid with a bag, a vegetable vendor, a family in a car. He glances at each quickly and waves most through, but places a small red flag card on two visitors and points them toward a side office. In that side office, through an open door, a senior security officer, a grey-haired retired army man with a moustache and a clipboard, sits at a desk and questions the two flagged visitors closely, examining an ID card under a lamp. On the gate cabin wall, a printed list of rules is written in one language only; a visitor in the queue speaks in a different language and the guard looks unsure, hinting that rules trained in one language may miss others. Warm late-afternoon light, alert but routine mood. Labels: "CHEAP CHECK ON ALL" above the gate guard, "CLOSE REVIEW" above the side office.

key: makes excellent chai (domain skill)
name: ch04_chaiwala_ignores_instruction
alt: A customer asks for a small cutting chai with less sugar in a paper cup, but the chaiwala serves a full glass of very sweet chai, and a billing machine rejects the unexpected order.
scene: A roadside chai stall at a busy office corner in the morning. On the left, a customer, a young woman in a formal kurta with an office bag, raises one finger and speaks, her speech bubble showing three small icons: a half-filled small glass, a sugar spoon crossed out, and a paper cup. In the centre, the chaiwala, a skilled man in his 40s with a towel on his shoulder, pours a perfect long stream of frothy chai from a height, clearly an expert; but he hands over a full tall glass with three sugar cubes drawn floating above it, smiling proudly. The customer's face shows mild dismay. On the right, a small modern billing machine attached to the stall shows only two buttons, one for cutting and one for full; a paper chit reading "a nice big glass" has been fed into it and the screen shows a red error symbol with sparks. A queue of office workers waits behind her holding coins. Bright morning light, steam rising, slightly comic mood. Labels: "GREAT CHAI" above the chaiwala, "WRONG ORDER" above the glass, "FORMAT ERROR" on the billing machine.

key: A Ramlila actor playing Hanuman
name: ch04_ramlila_actor_in_character
alt: A Ramlila actor playing Hanuman on an open-air stage stays in character, while a thought bubble shows the forbidden modern topics he must not mention.
scene: An open-air Ramlila stage on a festival night in a north Indian town, viewed from the audience. On the stage, decorated with painted backdrops of a forest and a palace, an actor in a full Hanuman costume with a mace, a golden crown and a long tail speaks dramatically in a deep heroic voice, a speech bubble with old-style flourishes. Around his head floats a large thought bubble crossed out with a red line, containing things he must never mention: a cricket scoreboard, a smartphone with chat bubbles and a television set. Below the stage, the audience of families sits on durries, children at the front with wide eyes, and an elderly man in a shawl watches very closely, ready to spot any slip. In the wings, a director with a script and a torch holds up a hand-written list of forbidden topics as a reminder. Strings of bulbs and smoke from a dhoop stand create a warm festive glow, and a drummer at the side of the stage keeps the rhythm. Labels: "STAY IN CHARACTER" above the stage, "MUST NOT KNOW" on the crossed-out thought bubble.

key: fixed monthly cost (EMI, insurance
name: ch04_app_cab_vs_own_car_cost
alt: Split illustration: an app cab costs the same per ride however often you ride, while an owned car has a fixed monthly cost that gets cheaper per trip the more you drive.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same young professional woman in her 30s with a laptop bag in both halves. LEFT panel: she stands at a kerb with her phone as an app cab pulls up; above her, a row of identical coins hovers over a row of small taxi icons, one coin per ride, whether one ride or fifty. A month calendar beside her shows each ride as a coin, the pile growing evenly. RIGHT panel: she stands beside her own small car in a residential parking spot; above the car, a fixed stack of bills is shown, for loan instalment, insurance and a driver's salary, the same each month; next to it, a simple bar shows the cost of each trip shrinking as the number of trips on the calendar grows. In the far corner of the right panel, a mechanic and two engineers in overalls work late at night with torches under a large server-like machine in the garage, a hint that owning has its own crew to keep it running. Bright daylight on the left, warm evening light on the right. Labels: "PAY PER RIDE" above the left panel, "FIXED COST" above the right panel.

key: Choosing a college: first drop
name: ch04_choosing_college_funnel
alt: A student choosing a college through a funnel: dropping colleges outside city or budget, shortlisting by a national ranking, visiting campuses, and keeping a check after joining.
scene: A large funnel drawn across the scene from top to bottom, with a seventeen-year-old girl in a T-shirt and jeans and her father in a half-sleeve shirt standing beside it with a laptop and a folder of brochures. At the wide top of the funnel, dozens of small college building icons pour in. FIRST stage: a sieve with a map pin and a rupee symbol knocks out colleges outside their city or budget, which tumble off to the side. SECOND stage: a printed ranking list on a clipboard shortlists a handful by their position. THIRD stage: a small scene of the girl and her father walking on a leafy campus, talking to two senior students in the canteen about their branch. BOTTOM of the funnel: one college gate with the girl walking in with a backpack, and beside her a small notebook titled with a checkmark icon where she keeps noting how things go after joining. Bright hopeful daylight, family decision mood. Labels: "HARD FILTERS" at the first stage, "LEADERBOARD" at the second stage, "OWN EVALUATION" at the third stage.

key: buying a sealed, ready-to-eat biryani
name: ch04_sealed_biryani_vs_recipe
alt: Split illustration: a sealed ready-to-eat biryani pack without recipe, versus the same biryani with its full recipe and supplier list, each with a different licence label.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, a kitchen counter in both halves. LEFT panel: a sealed foil pack of ready-to-eat biryani sits on the counter, being reheated in a pan by a young man in a T-shirt who adds a bowl of raita beside it; the pack has no ingredient list, and a thought bubble above him shows a question mark over a sack of rice and a spice tin. RIGHT panel: the same biryani in a handi, accompanied by a thick handwritten recipe book open to the biryani page and a folded supplier list showing a rice farm, a spice market and a dairy; a home chef in an apron reads the recipe with interest. On both packs, a large tag hangs like a label, with tiny icons: a house for home use only, a large restaurant with many tables marked with a stop hand, and a chef's hat crossed out. In the corner of the right panel, a heap of glowing computer chips and money bags hints that cooking the recipe from scratch costs a fortune. Warm kitchen light. Labels: "OPEN WEIGHTS" above the left panel, "OPEN MODEL" above the right panel, "LICENSE" on the hanging tag.

key: served by the original restaurant
name: ch04_same_recipe_many_kitchens
alt: The same famous recipe is served by the original restaurant, a mall food court, a cloud kitchen and a home cook, each giving a slightly different taste and portion.
scene: A four-quadrant illustration, each quadrant showing the same famous dish, a plate of butter chicken with naan, made from the same recipe card pinned at the centre where the four quadrants meet. TOP LEFT: the original restaurant with a heritage signboard and a waiter in a turban serving a generous portion. TOP RIGHT: a mall food court counter with plastic trays and a smaller portion in a disposable box. BOTTOM LEFT: a cloud kitchen with stainless-steel counters and a delivery rider picking up a sealed box. BOTTOM RIGHT: a home kitchen with a young couple cooking it themselves, the colour of the curry a little paler. Each plate has a small taste meter next to it with a needle at a slightly different position. A diner in the centre, a woman in her 30s holding a spoon, tastes from each with a thoughtful face. In a separate small inset at the top, a locked recipe box with a key held by just one restaurant and one partner shows the secret recipe served only by its owner. Warm, varied lighting in each quadrant. Labels: "SAME RECIPE" on the central card, "TASTE AGAIN" near the diner, "SECRET RECIPE" on the inset.

key: account books to an outside CA firm
name: ch04_ca_firm_books_stolen_phone
alt: Split illustration: a shopkeeper handing his account books to an outside accounting firm while a state border sign forbids some records leaving, and a buyer questioned by police over a stolen second-hand phone.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a shopkeeper in his 50s in a kurta and white boat-shaped cap hands a thick red account ledger across the desk to an outside accounting firm's young partner in a suit; behind the partner, filing cabinets and a photocopier, and a faint dotted line suggests copies might be made. At the edge of the panel, a road sign at a state border shows a small document with a stop hand, meaning certain records cannot leave. RIGHT panel: a crowded street market of second-hand phones, a young man in a hoodie buys a used phone from a stall; in the next moment, shown just behind, a policeman in khaki taps the same young man on the shoulder while the stall seller has vanished, and the phone glows with a small warning symbol and a chain of past owners drawn as faint silhouettes trailing back into the crowd. The shopkeeper looks back over his shoulder, uneasy. Office tones on the left, busy market light on the right. Labels: "DATA PRIVACY" above the left panel, "DATA LINEAGE" above the right panel.

key: Choosing a phone using reviews
name: ch04_phone_reviews_different_tests
alt: A buyer compares phone reviews from different sites, one testing camera, one battery and one gaming, and the camera winner loses on battery.
scene: A young buyer in his 20s with a backpack stands in a mobile phone shop, holding up three printed review pages fanned out in his hand, with three phones displayed on the glass counter in front of him. Above him, three review stands are drawn like small judging booths, each run by a reviewer with a different test: the first reviewer with a camera on a tripod photographs a flower vase, the second holds a stopwatch beside a phone plugged into a battery tester, and the third plays a game on a phone with headphones on. Each booth has its own little trophy on a different phone. One phone wins the camera trophy but sits at the bottom of the battery chart, a red low-battery icon glowing on it. In the corner, a fourth booth is empty with a closed sign, because that test is expensive to run. The shopkeeper behind the counter, a man in a polo shirt, waits patiently. Bright shop lighting with glowing display screens, slightly overwhelmed mood. Labels: "CAMERA" above the first booth, "BATTERY" above the second booth, "GAMING" above the third booth.

key: Your favourite restaurant changes chefs
name: ch04_restaurant_new_chef_mixed
alt: A restaurant changes chefs, and biryani regulars complain while dosa regulars celebrate, both correct for their own dish.
scene: A popular family restaurant dining hall viewed from the entrance. Through the kitchen's service window at the back, an old chef with a white beard is seen leaving through the rear door with his bag, while a new young chef in a crisp white uniform steps in and ties his apron. In the dining hall, two groups of regular customers sit at separate tables. On the left, a table of biryani lovers, an elderly man and his family, push their plates away with frowns, a speech bubble showing a down arrow over a biryani pot. On the right, a table of dosa fans, a group of college students, raise their crispy dosas happily, a speech bubble showing an up arrow over a dosa. In the centre, the restaurant owner stands between the tables with a confused, helpless expression. A small inset at the top right shows a closed kitchen door with a blank sign, meaning a customer may not even see that the chef changed. Warm restaurant lighting with ceiling fans, mixed emotional mood. Labels: "WORSE FOR ME" above the left table, "BETTER FOR ME" above the right table.

key: A train journey from Delhi to Chennai
name: ch04_train_per_segment_delays
alt: A train route from Delhi to Chennai with each station stop checked, showing the final arrival is ten hours late and the per-segment log pinpointing where the delay happened.
scene: A long horizontal railway route map spanning the image from a northern city on the left to a southern coastal city on the right, with a long passenger train traveling along it. Major stations along the line are marked with small circles and station boards: the start, then Nagpur, then Vijayawada, then the destination. At each station, a small inspector in a black coat holds a clipboard and ticks boxes for on-time and clean. At the destination on the right, a big station clock and a displeased passenger family standing with luggage show the train arriving ten hours late. Below the route, a long strip like a ledger shows each segment as a bar, and one segment between Nagpur and Vijayawada is far longer and coloured red, with a magnifying glass over it, pinpointing where the delay happened. A small inset of the destination-only check, a single ticket stamped late, sits in the corner looking unhelpful on its own. Morning light over fields and hills along the route, travel mood. Labels: "PER-TURN" above the station inspectors, "TASK-BASED" above the destination clock, "DELAY HERE" on the red segment.

key: strike rate above 130 in T20
name: ch04_selector_t20_rubric
alt: A cricket selector judges a batter who scored 40 off 45 balls against a written rubric for strike rate and finishing, ruling it correct but not good for T20.
scene: A cricket selectors' room in a stadium pavilion, glass windows overlooking a match in progress. On a large screen, a batter in coloured clothing is shown walking off after making 40 runs from 45 balls, his score glowing on the screenboard. At the long table, a chief selector in his 60s in a blazer and two other selectors examine a printed one-page rubric with three rows: a speedometer icon with a minimum strike-rate line, two arrows rotating for strike rotation, and a falling wicket crossed out for the last over. The batter's numbers are being checked row by row with ticks and crosses: runs scored has a tick, strike rate has a red cross. One selector holds up a scorebook showing the runs and gives a so-so hand gesture. A tea tray and a stack of player files sit on the table, and a whiteboard behind them lists the qualities wanted for the T20 squad. Bright afternoon light through the windows, serious evaluation mood. Labels: "CORRECT" beside the runs tick, "NOT GOOD ENOUGH" beside the strike-rate cross, "RUBRIC" on the printed sheet.

key: re-picking 100 laddoos from the same box
name: ch04_laddoo_bootstrap_simpson
alt: A taster samples laddoos from one box repeatedly to see if the rating jumps, while two sweet shops show one winning on each sweet but losing overall because of what each mostly sold.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a food inspector in a white cap and apron stands beside a big box of a hundred laddoos; she repeatedly draws handfuls into a small tray, sometimes picking the same laddoo twice, shown by a dotted loop arrow back to the box; beside her, a row of five small rating cards from repeated draws shows similar but slightly varying numbers, and a little wobble meter shows how much the rating jumps. RIGHT panel: two sweet shops side by side, Shop A and Shop B; above each, two small trophies show Shop A winning both the laddoo and jalebi tastings. But Shop A's counter is piled high mostly with jalebis, the harder item, while Shop B's counter is piled mostly with laddoos; a big overall scoreboard above them surprisingly shows Shop B ahead, and a confused customer scratches his head. Glass jars of sweets line the shelves behind. Warm sweet-shop lighting, marigold garlands. Labels: "BOOTSTRAP" above the left panel, "SIMPSON'S PARADOX" above the right panel.

key: An experienced auto driver understands
name: ch05_auto_driver_spellings
alt: Split illustration: an experienced auto driver understands three spellings of the same station as one place, while a new driver with a weak map app goes to three different places.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves on a busy Mumbai street with yellow-and-black auto-rickshaws. LEFT panel: an experienced auto driver in his 50s with a grey moustache, khaki uniform and a towel on his shoulder leans out of his auto; three different passengers hold up three phones each showing a slightly different spelling of the same station name, one short, one abbreviated, one long with extra words; three arrows from the phones all converge into one single station building drawn ahead, and the driver gives a relaxed nod. RIGHT panel: a young new driver in a fresh uniform squints at a cheap phone mounted on his dashboard with a glitchy map; the same three spellings lead to three diverging arrows ending at three different places, a station, a market and a hospital, and a confused passenger in the back throws up her hands. Bright humid daylight, honking traffic in the background. Labels: "STRONG MODEL" above the left panel, "WEAK MODEL" above the right panel.

key: A new helper at a kirana shop
name: ch05_kirana_helper_example_bills
alt: A new helper at a kirana shop looks at two example bills written by the owner and writes the third bill in the same format, with no billing course.
scene: Inside a small kirana shop with shelves of packets, sacks of rice and a hanging scale, viewed from behind the counter. The owner, a cheerful man in his 50s in a white vest and spectacles, has placed two handwritten bills on the counter, each listing a couple of grocery items with quantities and an arrow to a total. Beside them, a new helper, a teenage boy in a T-shirt and a cap, bends over a third blank bill and copies the same format exactly, pencil in hand, his eyes darting between the two examples; dotted lines connect the columns of the example bills to the matching columns of his bill. On the wall behind them, a poster for a billing course is crossed out, he never went to one. A customer, a woman with a cloth shopping bag, waits with items on the counter. In a small inset at the corner, the next morning, the same helper stares at a blank bill with a puzzled face, the two examples gone from the counter. Warm tube light and late afternoon glow. Labels: "TWO EXAMPLES" above the owner's bills, "IN-CONTEXT LEARNING" above the helper.

key: Teaching your nephew a new card game
name: ch05_card_game_zero_vs_few_shot
alt: An uncle teaches a card game: the teenage nephew learns from the rules alone, the younger nephew needs two sample hands, and an unusual regional game needs a sample hand even for the teenager.
scene: A family living room on a winter evening, a durrie on the floor, cushions and a plate of peanuts. An uncle in his 40s in a sweater sits cross-legged with a deck of cards. Three moments are shown left to right across the floor. LEFT: a sharp teenage nephew in a hoodie listens to the uncle read rules from a small card, and immediately plays well, a light bulb above his head. MIDDLE: a younger nephew of about seven, in pyjamas, watches the uncle lay out two sample hands face up on the durrie, numbered 1 and 2, before trying himself with a big smile. RIGHT: the uncle unwraps an unusual old regional card deck with strange symbols, and even the teenage nephew frowns until the uncle shows one sample hand. In the background, a coin jar labelled with a rupee symbol has a coin dropped in each time a sample hand is shown, a hint that examples cost something each time. Warm lamp light, cosy family mood. Labels: "ZERO-SHOT" above the left moment, "FEW-SHOT" above the middle moment, "UNUSUAL GAME" above the right moment.

key: The briefing the station master gave
name: ch05_station_master_system_prompt
alt: A station master briefs an enquiry clerk in the morning with standing rules, and later passengers ask their own questions at the clerk's window.
scene: A two-part illustration of a railway station enquiry office. LEFT part, early morning with mist outside: the station master, a dignified man in his 50s in a white uniform with a cap and brass badges, stands in the office and briefs a young enquiry clerk in a blue shirt, holding up three fingers; a speech bubble shows three small icons: a smiling face, a train, and a phone with a crossed-out line. The clerk nods and writes on a notepad pinned above his desk. RIGHT part, busy daytime: the same clerk sits behind the glass window with the notepad still pinned behind him, while a queue of passengers asks questions one by one through the speaking hole, a student with a backpack, a grandmother with a bundle, a businessman with a briefcase, each with their own speech bubble about trains. One passenger at the end of the queue leans in with a sly smile and a bubble showing a phone, trying to talk the clerk out of his briefing. Soft morning mist on the left, bright busy light on the right. Labels: "SYSTEM PROMPT" above the station master, "USER PROMPTS" above the queue.

key: A bank cheque. The amount, date
name: ch05_cheque_layout_chat_template
alt: Two bank cheques with different layouts, one filled correctly in the expected boxes and one with the amount written in the payee box, accepted silently with worse results.
scene: A bank counter viewed from the customer side, with a glass partition and a cashier in a tie. On the counter lie two oversized cheques side by side, each from a different bank with a different box layout: one with the date box on the top right, the other with the date box on the top left. A customer, a woman in her 40s in a printed sari, has filled the first cheque perfectly, with the date, amount in words, amount in figures and signature each sitting neatly inside the right boxes, marked by small ticks. On the second cheque, a young man in a hoodie has written the amount inside the payee box and the name in the amount box; the cashier squints at it, shrugs and stamps it anyway, and the cash he hands over is visibly less than expected, a small sad face drawn on the notes. A layout guide card for each bank stands in a little holder on the counter. A queue of customers with passbooks waits behind them. Fluorescent bank lighting, mildly cautionary mood. Labels: "CHAT TEMPLATE" above the cheques, "WRONG BOX" on the misfilled cheque.

key: A school assembly. The principal
name: ch05_school_assembly_principal
alt: A school assembly where students attend more to the principal's opening announcement than to a student's comment in the middle, and a prankster imitates the principal's voice.
scene: A morning school assembly in an open courtyard, viewed from behind the rows of students in uniform standing in lines. On a raised platform at the front, the principal, a dignified woman in her 50s in a starched cotton sari and spectacles, speaks into a microphone at the start of the assembly; thick bold attention lines flow from every student's head toward her, and her speech bubble is drawn large. Later in the assembly, in the middle of the lines, a student raises his hand and speaks a comment, and only a few thin attention lines point to him. At the back of the courtyard, a prankster boy with spiky hair cups his hands and imitates the principal's voice, drawn as a speech bubble with the same bold border as hers, and a few students turn their heads, unsure who is speaking. A flag pole and a banyan tree frame the scene. Bright early-morning sunlight with long shadows, orderly but slightly mischievous mood. Labels: "SYSTEM PROMPT" above the principal, "USER" above the middle student, "IMITATION" above the prankster.

key: In 2019 it was a sticky note
name: ch05_cheat_sheet_to_cupboard
alt: An exam cheat sheet growing from a sticky note in 2019 to a whole cupboard of books in 2024, with a student unable to find the page she needs.
scene: A two-part illustration of the same exam hall desk five years apart. LEFT part, labelled with a small year tag reading "2019": a student in a school uniform has a single yellow sticky note stuck to the corner of her desk with a few formulas on it, and she writes calmly. RIGHT part, with a year tag reading "2024": the same desk now has a huge wooden cupboard stuffed full of thick books standing beside it, doors open, books spilling out; the same student, now a young woman in a college hoodie, stands on her chair digging through the shelves, papers flying, unable to find the one page she needs, while the exam clock on the wall ticks down. A small meter on the cupboard shows a rupee symbol and an hourglass, each growing with the number of books. An invigilator in a cardigan walks between the rows, and other students nearby are also buried in their own cupboards. Calm light on the left, frantic light on the right. Labels: "SMALL WINDOW" above the left part, "HUGE WINDOW" above the right part, "WHERE IS IT?" in a thought bubble above the searching student.

key: Watch the ball, play late, keep
name: ch05_batting_hack_vs_fundamentals
alt: Split illustration: one batter tapping his bat twice for luck as a personal hack, versus a coach teaching many batters across generations to watch the ball and keep the head still.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves at cricket nets. LEFT panel: a single batter in a helmet taps his bat twice on the crease with an exaggerated superstitious expression, a little horseshoe and four-leaf clover drawn faintly above his head; a scorecard next to him shows one lucky innings, while two other batters watching try the same tapping and get bowled, stumps flying. RIGHT panel: a calm veteran coach in a tracksuit with a whistle shows three batters of different ages, a boy, a young woman and an older man, the same three fundamentals drawn as simple icons on a board: an eye following a ball, a clock showing a late shot, and a head held level with a spirit-level bubble; faded photos on the pavilion wall behind show players from earlier generations doing the same. A bowling machine and a bucket of balls stand at the end of each net, and a younger player sits on a kitbag taking notes. Bright morning sun on green turf. Labels: "HACK" above the left panel, "FUNDAMENTALS" above the right panel.

key: paint the walls off-white, ceiling white
name: ch05_painter_clear_instructions
alt: Split illustration: a painter told only to paint the room nicely paints everything including the wooden door, versus a painter given exact instructions that leave nothing to guess.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same apartment room and the same painter, a wiry man in his 40s in paint-splattered clothes with a cap made of newspaper, in both halves. LEFT panel: the homeowner, a woman in her 30s, waves her hand vaguely with a speech bubble showing only a smiley face; the painter has painted the walls bright orange and has also painted over the beautiful carved wooden door, which drips with orange paint; the homeowner covers her mouth in shock. RIGHT panel: the homeowner hands the painter a clear written list with four lines, each with a small icon: an off-white wall swatch, a white ceiling swatch, two brush strokes for two coats, and a wooden door crossed out with a red line; the painter works neatly, and masking tape protects the wooden door, which stays its natural brown. A ladder, paint tins and drop sheets in both halves. Soft daylight through a window. Labels: "VAGUE" above the left panel, "SPECIFIC" above the right panel, "DO NOT TOUCH" on the door.

key: Grandma says 10/10; the art teacher
name: ch05_drawing_three_judges
alt: A child's drawing is judged by a grandmother giving full marks, an art teacher giving six and an art critic giving two, showing how a persona sets the standard.
scene: A bright living room with a child's crayon drawing of a house, a sun and a lopsided cow pinned in the centre of the wall like an exhibit. A proud seven-year-old girl in a frock with crayon-stained fingers stands beside it. Three judges stand in a row in front of the drawing, each holding up a score card. LEFT: a beaming grandmother in a soft cotton sari with her hands clasped, her card showing 10 out of 10 with little hearts around it. MIDDLE: an art teacher in her 30s with a jhola bag and a pencil behind her ear, studying the proportions with one eye closed and her thumb raised, her card showing 6 out of 10. RIGHT: a stern art critic in a black turtleneck and round glasses, holding a notebook and frowning slightly, his card showing 2 out of 10. Above the three judges, three different measuring tapes hang from the ceiling, each with different markings, to show different standards. The girl looks from one card to the next, puzzled. Warm afternoon sunlight from a window, gently humorous mood. Labels: "SAME DRAWING" above the pinned drawing, "PERSONA" above the row of judges.

key: Training a new waiter at a family
name: ch05_waiter_magic_ice_cream_example
alt: A restaurant manager teaches a new waiter the right tone with one example about magic ice cream, and a short menu board line shows a compact format.
scene: A cheerful family restaurant during a quiet afternoon before the evening rush, viewed from beside the dessert counter. The manager, a friendly woman in her 40s in a smart kurta with a name badge, demonstrates to a nervous new waiter, a young man in a black vest and bow tie. On the left, she acts out the example: a small girl with pigtails at a nearby table points at a bowl of colourful ice cream and asks if it is magic, and the manager bends down with a wink and sparkles drawn around the bowl, the child gasping with delight. The new waiter watches, a light bulb above his head, while a thick binder of rules lies closed and ignored on the counter. On the right, a chalkboard menu on the wall shows a short compact line with an item and a price separated by an arrow, while beside it a cluttered alternative version with long labels is crossed out. Other waiters set tables in the background. Warm afternoon light through big windows, playful mood. Labels: "ONE EXAMPLE" above the manager and child, "SHORT FORMAT" beside the chalkboard.

key: The blank line tells you exactly where
name: ch05_form_signature_blank_line
alt: Split illustration: a form with a labelled signature line where a person signs in the right place, versus a form with no label where people sign anywhere or keep writing in the previous field.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a government office counter with a pen on a chain and a large printed form. LEFT panel: the form ends with a clear printed label and a blank line beneath it; a middle-aged man in a checked shirt and reading glasses signs neatly right on the line, and a clerk behind the counter nods, stamping it. A bright arrow points from the label to the line. RIGHT panel: the same form but the label and line have been removed, leaving an empty unmarked space after the address field; three different people have filled it: one signed diagonally across the address, another continued writing his address into the blank area, and a third signed in the margin upside down; the clerk holds the form up with a puzzled face. A queue of applicants with folders waits in both halves, and a stack of rejected forms grows on the right. Fluorescent office light, ceiling fan, wooden counter. Labels: "CLEAR MARKER" above the left panel, "NO MARKER" above the right panel.

key: open the ledger first (right)
name: ch05_society_secretary_ledger
alt: Split illustration: a housing society secretary guessing a resident's maintenance due from memory and getting it wrong, versus opening the ledger first and getting it right.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in a small housing society office with a notice board, a steel cupboard and a ceiling fan. A resident, a young woman in office clothes with a laptop bag, stands at the desk asking her question. LEFT panel: the society secretary, a retired gentleman in his 60s in a white kurta and spectacles, leans back in his chair, eyes rolled up, guessing from memory; his speech bubble shows a number with a big red cross over it, and the resident frowns. RIGHT panel: the same secretary opens a thick maintenance ledger on the desk, running his finger down the row for her flat number, and a green-ticked number appears in his speech bubble; the resident smiles and takes out her phone to pay. In the right panel, a faint thought bubble still floats above his head with his old remembered number, hinting that memory can still mix in. Warm afternoon light through a window grille. Labels: "FROM MEMORY" above the left panel, "CONTEXT" on the open ledger.

key: playing a 1950s village teacher
name: ch05_period_actor_slips
alt: An actor playing a 1950s village teacher in a period film slips during a long improvised scene and mentions messaging someone, as the director winces.
scene: A film set built as a 1950s Indian village schoolroom: mud walls, a slate blackboard, wooden benches, a hand-cranked bell and a hurricane lantern. Child actors in old-fashioned shorts and frocks sit on the floor with slates. The lead actor, a man in his 40s dressed as the village teacher in a dhoti, a khadi kurta, a white boat-shaped cap and round spectacles, stands at the blackboard mid-scene. His speech bubble begins with old-style words, but at the end a small modern phone icon appears with a message bubble, an obvious slip. Behind the camera, the director in a cap with a megaphone slaps his forehead, and a script supervisor holds up a crossed-out phone sign. In a thought bubble behind the actor's head, a modern smartphone glows faintly, showing he cannot un-know phones. Rehearsal call sheets and a clapperboard lie on a chair in the foreground. Warm lantern-like film lighting with a few studio lights visible at the edges. Labels: "PERIOD ROLE" above the schoolroom, "SLIP" next to the phone icon.

key: A line of cooks (one for rotis
name: ch05_wedding_kitchen_line_of_cooks
alt: Split illustration: one cook struggling to make an entire wedding meal alone, versus a line of cooks for rotis, dal and sweets working in parallel and a plate assembled at the end.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in a wedding catering tent behind the main hall. LEFT panel: a single overwhelmed cook in a vest and lungi juggles a tawa of rotis, a pot of dal and a kadhai of gulab jamuns all at once; smoke rises, a roti burns and dal boils over, and a long line of waiters waits with empty plates. RIGHT panel: three cooks in white aprons stand at three separate stations in a row: one rolling and flipping rotis, one stirring a big pot of dal, one frying sweets; the roti and sweet stations work at the same time, shown by matching clock icons. A supervisor tastes the dal and points directly at its cook with a speech bubble showing a salt shaker, easy to tell who to fix. At the end of the line, a steel thali plate is assembled with all three items, and a guest at the hatch waits until the whole plate is ready. Marigold garlands hang at the tent entrance. Warm firelight and busy steam. Labels: "ONE COOK" above the left panel, "PROMPT CHAIN" above the right panel.

key: Students who write each step
name: ch05_show_your_working
alt: Split illustration: a student jumping straight to an answer and getting it wrong, versus a student writing each step and checking answers in the last ten minutes.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in a school maths exam hall with wooden desks and a large wall clock. On the blackboard behind both students, the teacher has written an instruction with a small arrow icon of steps. LEFT panel: a boy in a uniform scribbles a single answer under a long word problem without any working, a quick confident grin, and a red cross appears beside it; a tiny thought bubble shows him skipping a staircase by jumping. RIGHT panel: a girl in a uniform writes each step on her answer sheet in a neat column, like climbing a staircase one step at a time, arriving at a correct answer with a green tick; in a small inset at the corner, the wall clock shows the last ten minutes and she goes back over her steps with a pencil, circling and fixing one small slip before time ends. An invigilator walks between the rows. Bright morning light through tall windows. Labels: "JUMP TO ANSWER" above the left panel, "SHOW YOUR WORKING" above the right panel, "SELF-CHECK" on the inset.

key: change one thing at a time, write it
name: ch05_sambar_one_change_notebook
alt: A cook changes the sambar recipe one thing at a time, records each change in a notebook, and has the family taste the whole meal so the sambar does not clash with the rasam.
scene: A South Indian home kitchen and dining area, viewed from the doorway. On the left, a young man in a T-shirt with an apron stirs a pot of sambar on a gas stove; beside him a small spice tray shows a single extra pinch of tamarind being added, while every other ingredient sits untouched with a small lock icon. On the kitchen counter, an open notebook shows a neat table with dated rows, each row recording just one change and a family rating. On the right, in the dining area, the whole family sits on the floor around banana leaves: grandmother, parents and a younger sister, each tasting a complete meal of rice, sambar, rasam, poriyal and papad, not just the sambar.
